title: Schedule a held email for a date and time
description: A held outbound email now has Schedule beside Approve, Edit and Discard. Pick a date and time, and it sends then. Until it does, Send now and Discard still work.

title: Spell check and autocorrect in the Mac app
description: Every text box in the Mac app now checks spelling and corrects as you type. Edit > Spelling and Grammar and Edit > Substitutions let you turn each one off. Smart quotes and dashes stay off, so a command you send to a worker is not altered.

title: Cmd-K shows which workers and tabs are already open
description: The Cmd-K list marks the worker on this page as Open here, and a worker or tab open elsewhere in the Mac app as Open. Choosing it takes you there.

title: Workers can message people one to one
description: A direct message from a worker is listed with your people and opens as a 1:1 conversation. Your own entry opens too, and an image link of any common format previews inline.

title: OpenCode workers take steering, interrupts and live model switches
description: amux now drives OpenCode through its own server API, so you can steer and interrupt an OpenCode worker, switch its model while it runs, and apply the same worker boundaries.

title: A new device with the right password asks you in Needs you
description: When someone signs in to your server with the right password from an address it has not seen before, the sign-in is held and a card appears in your Needs you list. Allow adds that address for the account and lets them in; Dismiss leaves it blocked. A device you already allowed keeps working when its address changes.

title: amux help lists every command
description: Fifteen commands, including pause, resume, pin and version, worked but were missing from amux help. Each one now has a help line, and a check fails the build if a command and its help line ever drift apart again.

title: Message your workers from WhatsApp
description: Write @worker followed by a message in your WhatsApp chat with yourself, and amux delivers it to that worker. The worker's answer comes back to the same chat. Anything you write there without an @ stays a note to yourself.

title: Search Messages as you type
description: The Messages search box now finds results while you type, grouped into matching conversations and matching messages with your words highlighted. Chips for From, In, Time and Has narrow the search without typing operators, and Enter opens a full results page you can narrow to one conversation.

title: Double-tap the globe key to dictate in the Mac app
description: Tapping the globe key twice now starts dictation in the Mac app, and tapping it twice again stops it. The mic also starts listening right away instead of sitting on "Starting mic" while the app's storage catches up. If macOS is set to use the globe key for its own dictation, the app tells you once how to hand the key to amux.

title: Ask shows its closest matches under every answer
description: When you Ask a question about your message history, the three closest matching messages now appear under the answer with a short snippet each, as rows you can tap to open. You can check the source yourself even when the written answer is unsure.

title: The board records work and leaves your workers alone
description: Turning on a worker's Board switch now files and keeps its cards without typing reminders into the worker or starting tasks for it. Workers driven by a goal no longer get two drivers competing for their attention. Teams that want the board to hand out work can turn on AMUX_BOARD_STEERS for a worker, a group or everyone.

title: New /big-goal skill runs a large goal without you
description: Every install now ships /big-goal, which sets up a multi-day or multi-worker goal: a plan file with one owner per row, a checker per owner, a checked /goal on each worker and an hourly coordinator that reports one line. Use it when a goal is too big for a single /goal.

title: One worker can no longer close another worker's browser
description: If a worker joined another worker's browser in its own tab and the server restarted, its stop could close the whole shared browser. A worker's stop now only closes a browser it started, unless the request explicitly forces it.

title: Freeze a workspace in the Mac app
description: Window > Workspaces > Freeze Workspace (Option-Command-F) locks the tabs, names and workers in the open workspace so nothing gets closed, renamed or moved by accident. You can still resize windows, dividers and zoom. A frozen window says so under its title.

title: The Messages row menu stays open while the list updates
description: Live updates used to redraw the Messages list even when nothing changed, which closed an open row menu and could make Pin, Copy or Show answer miss. The list now redraws only on a real change and keeps the menu open.

title: See what a worker answered from the Messages menu
description: A message's row menu now has Show answer, which reads the worker's reply from its transcript. You can check what a worker said on your phone without opening a terminal, and a missing answer says why.

title: Every worker has Chat by default
description: Chat is now on for every worker unless you switch it off, including workers that already existed. Nothing runs until you send the first chat message, and workers that had it on are unchanged.

title: The board is opt-in per worker
description: A worker uses the shared board only when its own settings or its group turn a Board switch on. Workers without it no longer get every prompt filed as a card or receive board nudges.

title: Codex workers use the model in your Codex config
description: A Codex worker created with no model now uses the model set in your Codex config file. Before, amux passed its own default, which could fail on a ChatGPT login that codex handled fine when run directly.

title: A chip press runs the chip you see
description: Chips sync between devices, so the saved list could change after the bar rendered, and a press would run whatever chip now sat in that position. A press now runs the chip the bar shows.

title: Pin a message from a worker's Messages tab
description: A row's menu now pins or unpins a message, and a pin count opens the list of pinned messages. Choosing one puts its text in the composer, and each item has its own Unpin. Pins live on the server, so they follow the worker across your devices.

title: Your priorities outrank a card's age on the board
description: A P0 or P1 card now beats any older card when a worker picks its next task, so a two-day-old card no longer jumps ahead of an urgent one. A pin still leads, and age orders cards within a tier.

title: A board move the server refuses snaps back
description: Dragging a card used to leave it in the new column until a reload even when the server refused the move. The card now returns to its column and the toast says why. Offline and queued moves stay where you put them.

title: Schedules behave through the daylight saving change
description: When clocks fall back, the repeated hour no longer makes a schedule fire again and again. A daily or interval schedule set inside that hour now runs once and moves on to its next time.

title: A worker card shows when it last made progress
description: A worker on a long autonomous run used to read "WORKING 12h ago" because the card showed its last message. The card now shows the newer of the last message and the last progress.

title: A worker's status reaches its card at once
description: A change a worker reported took 6 to 12 seconds to show on its card, because the dashboard waited for the next full fleet update. Reports now appear right away.

title: The markdown editor keeps up with your typing on a phone
description: On a long note, each keystroke now takes about 17 ms on an iPhone instead of 178, switching to Edit is four times faster, and the note opens sooner. The editor redraws only the lines you changed, so typing and scrolling stay smooth on a phone.

title: Triage: captured tasks wait on the board until you accept them
description: Ask a worker to capture a task and it lands in Triage instead of being picked up on its own. A Triage chip leads the board's filter row, and amux board accept moves a card into the normal flow when you are ready, recording who accepted it and why.

title: Pin messages in a channel or DM
description: You or a worker can pin any post in a channel or DM you can read. Pins are listed per conversation, so the decision or link everyone needs stays at hand instead of scrolling away.

title: Usage & Optimization: see where your agent spend goes
description: A new Usage tab shows spend, cards finished and attempted, success rate and cost per success, broken down by group, plus a ranked list of changes that would save money, each with its evidence and an estimated monthly saving.

title: Cmd-K finds the files you open most
description: The command palette now searches files as well, ranked by how often and how recently you opened them, so the notes and docs you live in come up after a few letters.

title: Pause, resume or delete a worker's schedules together
description: A worker's Schedules tab now has checkboxes and a bulk bar, so you can pause, resume or delete several of its schedules at once without touching other workers' schedules.

title: An HTML folder opens as a website, and app links stay in the viewer
description: Open an HTML file from the Files tab and amux serves its whole folder as a website, with working links between pages, on a private address only you can open for 12 hours. Links inside an app now stay in the viewer instead of breaking out to a new tab, and an app whose session lapsed asks to reopen rather than showing an error.

title: A worker you @mention in Messages sees only its own thread
description: When you @mention a worker in a reply, it now gets that thread's earlier posts and nothing else, and a mention that starts a new thread arrives with no unrelated history. Workers answer the question you asked without picking up other conversations from the same channel.

title: The dashboard returns to live updates after a reconnect
description: After a few failed reconnects, for example during a deploy restart, a dashboard window fell back to polling the whole board every five seconds and never went back. It now keeps retrying the live stream and stops polling the moment it reconnects, which also clears a stuck Sync error pill when you come back online.

title: Deploys go live faster and roll back on their own
description: A new main commit goes live as soon as its fast checks pass, while the long end-to-end suite runs after the deploy. amux compiles the build while CI runs, and if the new build comes up unhealthy it rolls back to the last good one without anyone stepping in.

title: Storage tiers move idle folders to a cold drive and back
description: The Disk tab has a Storage tiers section: pick a cold drive, add folders to watch, and amux moves each folder to the drive when it sits idle and back when it is used. A link stays at the original path, so you and your agents keep using the same path and never see the move. Folders that keep growing are tiered one subfolder at a time.

title: A saved Mac workspace reopens on the right server
description: A workspace saved on one Mac used to reopen every tab on the other Mac's own localhost, which showed no workers. Saved workspaces and open windows now remember the server itself, so a workspace opens on the same amux server from any Mac that reaches it.

title: Click an attachment's icon to preview it
description: The icon on every attachment chip, in the worker input and on a worker card, now opens a preview: an image, video, audio, a PDF or the text of a text file. The preview reads your device's own copy while the upload is still running, so it never waits. Escape, the X or a click outside closes it, and on a phone the icon is a full 44px target.

title: Start a message from Messages, and @mention a worker to get it working in the thread
description: A pencil button in the Messages sidebar opens one picker over channels, people and workers, and keeps your draft when you pick. A worker you @mention in a direct message now answers in the thread under your post, as it already did in channels, and the rest of the conversation stays private. The message box is the same input you use to talk to a worker.

title: Owners and admins manage channels in Messages
description: The owner and admins can create a channel, rename it, make it private, archive or restore it, and add or remove people, from Manage channels at the end of the channel list or the settings button in a channel. Everyone else, workers included, is refused, and the buttons are hidden for them.

title: Recordings transcribe live and can write meeting notes
description: Live transcription is on by default: each open recording is transcribed in roughly 15-second pieces and saved as it goes, so a crash keeps every word so far, with your voice and the other side labelled You and Them. Opt in to meeting notes and amux writes a title, summary, decisions and action items with owners, followed by your own typed notes, and suggests which workers the meeting concerns.

title: A back button and recent places that take no extra row
description: Moving between tabs, workers, cards and files is now part of the browser history, so Back, a phone swipe and Cmd+[ return you to the last place in amux instead of leaving it. A small back arrow appears at the left of the header only when there is somewhere to go, and a long press or right click lists your last 15 places.

title: Queue social posts for a publish time, one publisher per platform, now with dev.to
description: Workers can queue a post for one or several platforms with a publish time, and amux checks every draft when it is queued so nothing is half-scheduled. A background job publishes due posts, retries a failure that reached nothing, and measures each post at 24 hours, 72 hours and 7 days. dev.to joins the supported platforms, and queued posts can be cancelled or rescheduled.

title: One timeline of everything a worker did in the browser and through its tools
description: Every browser step a worker takes is now logged with the page before and after, whether it loaded, any error and how long it took, with typed text, code and file paths never stored. Claude Code tool calls are recorded too, so you can triage a worker's browser use, tool use and API calls in one timeline.

title: Pass/fail schedules show a green Passing pill and lead with what the check found
description: A schedule whose pass check succeeds now reads Passing in green in the list and on its detail page, where it used to look like any other scheduled job. The detail view starts with the check's own one-line finding and keeps the shell command one tap away under How it's checked.

title: Messages grows into a team chat, with WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram and Discord bridged in
description: The Messages tab now works like a team chat: replies open threads, an @worker mention delivers the message with recent context, and posts can be edited, deleted, reacted to and searched. Voice notes are transcribed, link previews appear, and new posts reach every open client in about a third of a second, with native notifications on the Mac and iOS apps. A chat bridge links WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram or Discord chats to a worker or a group, and holds a worker's reply for your approval when a stranger is in the chat.

title: Open Word, PowerPoint and Excel files with their comments and tracked changes
description: The file view now renders Office documents natively. Word files show each page with commented ranges highlighted, insertions and deletions marked, and a panel listing every comment, reply and tracked change; click one to jump to it. PowerPoint decks render every slide with its speaker notes and comments, and Excel cell comments show as notes you can edit and save. On a phone, Word text reflows to the screen.

title: Eight skills ship with every amux install, including a new worker audit
description: slop, iterate, codex, muse, imessage, pr-merge, e2e-test and a new worker-audit now come with amux and install as Claude Code commands at boot. amux keeps its own copies current and never overwrites a copy you edited. /worker-audit reports whether chosen workers are turning time, tokens and attention into validated progress, and why not.

title: Recordings save to disk in pieces as you record, so a long one is never lost
description: The recorder now streams audio to the server in finished pieces while you record, instead of uploading one file at the end. A long recording survives closing the window or quitting the Mac app, gaps are detected, and a second window can no longer end the first one's recording. Transcription works on recordings past an hour.

title: The PR handler posts its own reviews, and a contributor's reply wakes it
description: The pull request watcher is now a closed loop. The handler posts one review or comment per new head commit, skips a PR that has not changed since its last verdict, and wakes again only when a contributor pushes or replies, never because of its own comment.

title: amux watch wakes a worker once when a file lands or a CI run finishes
description: Instead of hand-written polling loops, a worker can register a watch with amux watch add file or amux watch add ci. A per-worker shell schedule checks every watch each minute and delivers one message to the worker when a file appears, a CI run concludes, or the watch expires. Secret values are masked in the delivered text.

title: Schedule work for sunrise, sunset or after Shabbos
description: Schedules can now follow the sun: daily at sunset, every day at sunrise, every Saturday at sunset+50m, or simply after shabbos, which ends 50 minutes after Saturday sunset by default. Set AMUX_LATITUDE and AMUX_LONGITUDE in server.env and the times move with the season and your location. Without a location the scheduler refuses the expression and names the two settings to add.

title: Pass/fail schedules that re-run until the check passes
description: A schedule can now carry a pass check: a shell command whose exit code says whether the job really worked. After each run amux runs the check, and a failed schedule keeps being re-run until it passes. Turn on Pass/fail under Basic in the schedule editor and enter the check.

title: Every amux Cloud server follows main within minutes, with rollback
description: amux Cloud servers now pick up each new release within minutes instead of waiting for an hourly check. If a new build does not report healthy within five minutes, the server puts the previous version back and holds the bad one. Your Cloud server stays current without you doing anything.

title: Install the Mac app from a double-click .dmg
description: The amux Mac app now ships as a .dmg beside the zip on the desktop-latest release: open it and drag Amux to Applications. It is a universal app for macOS 12 and later. The app is not notarized yet, so macOS asks you to choose Open Anyway on first launch.

title: A Hotkeys tab, and ## to start dictation
description: A new Hotkeys tab lists every keyboard shortcut and text trigger in amux and lets you add your own. Type ## in any input to start dictating into it. Shortcuts that collide with another hotkey or a built-in are refused, and your list follows you across the browser, phone and Mac app.

title: Agents can download files through a signed-in browser profile
description: The browser automation can now download a file with the same sign-in as the page, so an agent can fetch a report or export from a site you are logged in to. Files land in ~/.amux/downloads/<session>/, up to 50 MB, and the reply gives the path, size and status. A response that is really a sign-in page is flagged instead of saved silently as the file.

title: An urgent alert opens the worker that raised it
description: When a worker sends an urgent alert, the text message now ends with a link that opens that worker in amux, and the email adds a link for the Mac app. Tap it on your phone and you land on the worker that needs you. If amux does not know its public address yet, the alert still goes out and says why it has no link.

title: 17 dependency advisories patched, plus a daily vulnerability watch
description: amux updated its TLS, HTTP/2, async runtime and spreadsheet libraries to close 17 published advisories, including the compromised certificate intermediates behind Tailscale's recent CVE. A new daily scheduled check audits main for new advisories and reports which ones affect what actually ships.

title: Another website cannot act on your amux server through your browser
description: amux now refuses any write or WebSocket connection that your browser marks as coming from a different site. On amux Cloud, where every server lives under amux.io, a page on one server could otherwise have made your browser send commands to another. The CLI, workers, webhooks and native apps are unaffected.

title: One Pages tab for internal apps, public apps and shared files
description: The Pages tab now lists three things in one place: apps only you can open inside amux, apps with a public link, and files or folders you chose to share. Add them from the tab or with amux publish. Nothing a worker adds opens until you approve it, and a shared page runs sandboxed so it cannot act as you.

title: Present a PDF or slide deck full screen
description: A Present button in the file viewer shows a PDF one page per screen in full screen, with keyboard, click and swipe navigation and clickable links. A PowerPoint, Keynote or ODP deck presents the PDF export saved beside it. Use it to walk a client through an agent's report from your laptop or iPad.

title: Filter Messages by several workers and groups at once
description: The global Messages tab has a picker with search and checkboxes for groups and workers, so you can read the conversation of a whole team or any mix of workers in one list. The button always shows what is applied, and opening Messages from a group's page preselects that group.

title: Post to YouTube from amux and track each video's results
description: Workers can upload a video to YouTube through amux and get the video id and link back, then amux reads its views and engagement at 24 hours, 72 hours and 7 days. Publishing publicly stays behind an owner switch. It closes the loop for agents that make and post marketing videos.

title: Send your amux change upstream with /amux-contribute
description: Type /amux-contribute followed by the change you want, and amux makes it in a fresh copy of main, checks it and opens a pull request to mixpeek/amux, from your fork if you cannot push upstream. You see the pull request before anything leaves your machine. /amux-contribute pull brings your copy back in line with the latest amux.

title: Cmd+K puts the best match first
description: The Cmd+K palette now ranks exact names and ids first, then prefix and whole-word matches, then text inside titles, then body text, then fuzzy matches. Within each group, busy workers and open cards rise and completed work sinks, while archived and discarded items stay hidden unless you ask for them.

title: Ask your amux database questions in plain English
description: The Database tab has a new Ask mode. Type a question, and amux writes one read-only SELECT, runs it and shows the SQL next to the rows, ready to copy, edit, re-run or open in the Query pane. Follow-up questions build on the earlier answers.

title: Open several files side by side
description: Right-click a file link, a Files row or a board artifact and choose Open in split view, and each file gets its own pane, so files sit side by side. A file already on screen is not added twice, and when every pane is in use the newest file takes the last pane.

title: Find, filter and step through every worker tab
description: The filter, up and down buttons and Find in the worker view header used to work only on the terminal. They now work on every tab: chat messages, schedules and their runs, logs, commits, board items and more. Find highlights matches and hides items without them, and the counter shows where you are.

title: Each pane in the Mac app has its own tabs
description: In the Mac app, every pane in a window now holds its own stack of tabs, up to four panes per window tab. Drop a tab in the middle of a pane to add it there, or on an edge to split. Tabs drag between panes, and closing a pane's last tab removes the pane.

title: amux Cloud uses your Claude subscription before an API key
description: When you sign in to Claude on amux Cloud and an API key in the environment has run out of credit, amux now uses your subscription for workers and helper tasks. Workers started before you signed in switch over at their next idle moment, on the same conversation.

title: Each worker tab shows that worker's data
description: Switching from one worker to another on the same tab could paint the first worker's answer onto the second when it arrived late. Ten tabs, including Memory, Git, Steering, Logs and Shell, now check that an answer still belongs to the worker on screen before showing it, so Save and Push always act on the worker you are looking at.

title: Drag a tab into the Mac app window to split it
description: In the amux Mac app, drag a tab over a window and a preview shows which half of the pane it will take. Drop it and the window becomes a grid of up to four panes, each keeping its page state, with dividers you can drag to resize.

title: See how much memory and CPU each worker uses
description: amux now samples each worker's memory, CPU and process count every 30 seconds and keeps seven days of history. The new Resources tab in Metrics shows live numbers and peaks per worker, and you can cap how many workers run at once and stagger their start after a reboot.

title: Claude sign-in on amux Cloud uses your subscription
description: Signing in to Claude from the dashboard now runs the same login as /login on a laptop. Your plan usage shows in the dashboard, and workers run on your Claude subscription instead of an API key.

title: Stuck queued messages can be retried or removed
description: A message saved on your device that never reached its worker used to sit in the Queued list with its buttons disabled. It now says what happened, and you can send it again or remove it.

title: A bigger terminal in the worker view on desktop
description: With a mouse and a wide screen, the header and command bar around a worker's terminal are tighter, so the terminal grows from 532 to 611 pixels tall at 1440 by 900. Touch screens keep the stacked layout.

title: More room for messages on your phone
description: A worker's Messages tab on a phone used about a third of the screen for search, filters and three header lines per message. The search row now fits, and each message takes far less space, so you read the conversation instead of the chrome around it.

title: Split view with two to four panes
description: Next to a worker's page you can now open one to three more panes, stacked. Each pane shows the same worker page on a view you pick from its dropdown, such as Chat, Terminal, Messages or Files, so you can watch a terminal while reading the conversation.

title: Fold the worker header to give the terminal room
description: Drag the grip under a worker's header upward and the header folds in stages: the toolbar moves up beside the name, then the extra lines collapse. In a short window that turns a one-line terminal into a usable one. The fold is saved per worker, so a saved workspace comes back the same way.

title: Refresh keeps you where you were
description: Reloading the dashboard now returns you to the worker, tab, card, file or view you were on. Before, a page opened from a link went back to that link on refresh, and every Mac app window went back to where it was at launch.

title: Update the Mac app from Settings
description: The Mac app has a new Settings > Updates panel. It checks the latest desktop release on GitHub, downloads it, verifies the bundle and its signature, swaps it in place and relaunches. No more downloading a zip by hand to stay current.

title: Attachments never block a send
description: If the browser's local storage stalls while saving an attached screenshot, amux now gives up on the local copy after a few seconds and uploads straight from memory. Before, the attachment could sit at Saving locally and the message could not be sent.

title: A lost message gets sent again
description: If a message you queued for a busy worker never reaches its transcript, amux notices and sends it once more. It used to count an empty message box as proof of delivery. A message still missing after the retry is logged as lost, never as delivered.

title: Pages: small web apps run by a worker
description: The new Pages tab hosts HTML apps at /pages/<name>, each with its own SQLite file and a worker that keeps it up to date. The page runs in a sandboxed frame and can only read and write its own database, ask its worker a question, or open a file. It respects your server's sign-in, Cloud included.

title: Snap windows and torn-off tabs into place on the Mac
description: In the Mac app, drag a window or a torn-off tab to a screen edge to snap it: the sides give half the screen, corners a quarter, the top fills it, and the bottom gives a third. A preview shows where it will land. Saved workspaces now keep each window's tab names.

title: Mac windows come back where you left them
description: The Mac app remembers each window's display, size, macOS Desktop, tabs and what it was showing, then restores them after a quit, crash, reboot or monitor change. Arrange workers across several Desktops once and keep that layout.

title: A terminal on both sides of split view
description: Split view now offers Terminal beside Files, Messages and Chat, so you can watch two terminals side by side. Each has its own message box, and the choice is remembered per worker.

title: Copy and paste in the terminal just work in the Mac app
description: Cmd+V in a worker's terminal now pastes into the message box without asking for clipboard permission, and Cmd+C copies a selection. Before, the Mac app blocked the paste and showed an error.

title: Queued messages no longer look delivered
description: A message still waiting in a worker's queue stays labeled as queued until the worker takes it. Switches such as the Board toggle in worker details now look and act like real on/off switches.

title: Mermaid diagrams draw wherever markdown shows
description: A mermaid code block in a note, a card, chat or the file viewer now draws as a diagram, in light or dark to match the theme. Mermaid loads only on pages that have a diagram. If a block does not parse, its source stays on screen with the reason.

title: Obsidian notes open in full, with working links
description: The file viewer renders Obsidian notes the way Obsidian does: wikilinks open the note or jump to the heading, and math and callouts render. Large notes no longer stop at 200,000 characters; text files open up to 5 million characters, and a cut says so.

title: Subscribe workers to events
description: Workers can subscribe to event patterns and act on a match: message a worker, create a board card, run a schedule or run a command. Match by event type, source and worker, with a dedupe window so one burst fires once. Manage subscriptions at /api/subscriptions and read the fire history at /api/subscriptions/fires.

title: Drag the message box taller
description: A grip on the message box's top-left corner lets you drag it taller, up to 70% of the screen, for long prompts. The size is kept per device, and a double-click resets it.

title: The Host strained dialog tells you what to do
description: When your machine is under load, the Host dialog now lists the biggest consumers first with one suggested step each: pause a busy worker with one button, or copy a command for a VM or another app. amux only pauses its own workers; for everything else it gives you the command to run.

title: Notifications open the card they are about
description: Tapping a needs-you notification on the Mac app, the PWA or in the dashboard now opens the board card it names, in the window you already have open. With work pending, tapping the status pill opens the status details too.

title: Markdown reads well on a phone
description: Tables in the file viewer wrap only between words and scroll sideways inside their frame, so cells no longer break mid-word. iPhone gets a draggable scroll thumb with a percentage, and diagrams open full screen.

title: Workers resume right after an account switch
description: When a worker hits a usage limit and amux switches to another Claude account, the worker now resumes at once even if a background shell from the old turn is still running. It also reads Claude Code's new Continuing shortly banner.

title: amux stop now stays stopped
description: Stopping a worker with amux stop is now recorded by the server, so the board's dispatcher no longer restarts it seconds later to pick up queued work. Every start also records who started it.

title: A faster dashboard on big fleets
description: The worker list the dashboard downloads dropped a quarter of its size, and board changes now arrive in one request instead of one per card. On a busy fleet the dashboard re-reads less and updates sooner.

title: Cmd-K finds any worker, card or tab by name
description: Press Cmd-K (Ctrl-K, or the search button on phones and iPads) for a Spotlight-style box that finds workers, groups, projects, tabs, actions, pins, vault entry names, connectors and skills. Type, use the arrow keys, and Enter opens it.

title: A native Mac app for amux
description: amux now has a native Mac app: several windows and tabs, a Dock badge and notifications when agents need you, a menu bar CPU and memory readout, pinned notes that float above other apps, and Control-Option-Space to show or hide it. Download Amux-macOS.zip from the GitHub release; it connects to your own server or your amux Cloud address.

title: Mac app: Settings and saved window layouts
description: The Mac app gains a Settings window (Cmd-,) and named window layouts that save every window, tab group and floating pin, then reopen them with one click. Choose what opens at launch: your last windows, one window, or a layout.

title: Manage billing or delete your Cloud account from Settings
description: amux Cloud owners now find "Manage billing or delete account" in their server's Settings, instead of having to know the amux.io billing page. Invited members never see it.

title: Sign in with your Claude subscription on amux Cloud
description: A new amux Cloud server now offers Sign in with Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini on first load, and the "No model connected" banner opens the same window. Before, a Cloud customer could only paste an API key.

title: The dashboard no longer reloads itself on a first visit
description: A fresh browser reloaded the dashboard about five seconds after opening it, which could wipe a sign-in window mid-flow on a new Cloud server. It now reloads only when newer dashboard code replaces older code.

title: Workers can save notes to their own amux memory
description: `amux memory add` appends a note to a worker's amux memory, the one the Memory tab shows, without overwriting what the owner saved. `amux memory` prints it.

title: Claude workers skip the first-run screens when you add a key later
description: On amux Cloud, saving an Anthropic key in the Vault after install left a new Claude worker stuck on Claude Code's first-run theme picker. amux now answers those screens at launch, so the first task runs.

title: Resubscribe within 30 days and get your Cloud server back
description: When you cancel amux Cloud, your server is kept as a snapshot for 30 days. Resubscribing with the same email now restores that server with its data, and the ready email says it was restored.

title: Cloud shows a restarting page instead of a blank error
description: If your amux Cloud server is restarting, you now see a page that says so, refreshes itself every 10 seconds, and gives hello@amux.io, instead of an empty 502.

title: Describe what you want, and a worker starts on it
description: The + button opens with one box: describe the outcome you want and press Cmd or Ctrl+Enter. amux starts a worker on a /goal that keeps going until the outcome is met. Group, folder, provider, model and constraints sit in a closed section with sensible defaults, and you can save them as yours.

title: Tasks pages link each stretch of work to its messages, cards and commits
description: Each worker and the fleet as a whole get a Tasks page. A task shows the messages sent during it, the board card it worked, the commits it landed on main and the requests it closed, and you can search across all of them.

title: A log search hit opens the terminal log at that line
description: Clicking a search result that points into a worker's terminal log now shows the lines around it, even from days ago, instead of only the loaded scrollback.

title: Disk tab recommends what to clean and writes the script for you
description: The Disk tab now shows free space, what is safe to remove, what needs review and what the scan never mapped. Findings are grouped by the tool that owns them, and a copyable cleanup script replaces deleting from the dashboard.

title: Schedules can end: start dates, end dates, run limits and owner locks
description: A schedule can wait until a start date, stop after an end date or a number of runs, and be locked by the owner so a worker cannot re-enable it. A disabled schedule records why.

title: Cap how many subagents a worker runs at once
description: A new subagents boundary refuses another subagent when a worker already runs its limit (4 by default) or the account is nearly out of usage headroom. The refusal says how many are running and when to retry.

title: Messages no longer cancel Claude's automatic continue after a usage limit
description: While Claude Code counts down to continue after a usage limit, amux holds incoming messages. Before, the Escape key sent ahead of a message cancelled the countdown and left the worker stopped.

title: Draw: rename and delete drawings, a default folder and safer autosave
description: Drawings and components can be renamed or deleted from the library, the selection bar has Delete with undo, new drawings go to a default folder you choose, and a failed autosave retries on its own.

title: Move a whole amux between your machine and amux Cloud
description: amux export writes one bundle with your board, schedules, memories and worker settings. amux import loads it into another amux, local or a Cloud server at yourname.amux.io, so you can start self-hosted and move to an always-on server without rebuilding anything.

title: Sign in with Apple finds your Cloud server in the iOS app
description: The iOS app's server picker has a Sign in with Apple button. It looks up the Cloud servers on your account and signs you in to the one you pick, with no URL to type.

title: Automatic Claude account switching is now opt-in
description: Switching a worker to another Claude account when one hits its usage limit is off by default. Turn it on with claude-rotate.py on or CLAUDE_ROTATE_ENABLED=1. Manual switching is unchanged.

title: Worker resource boundaries cover the shared network link
description: The resources boundary now includes network bandwidth alongside memory and CPU, so one agent pulling a large download cannot starve the rest of the fleet.

title: A saved OpenAI key signs Codex in before the worker starts
description: Codex workers no longer stop at a sign-in prompt when an OpenAI API key is already saved in amux. The key is applied before the worker launches.

title: Taps reach the dashboard on iPad
description: Fixed an overlay that swallowed taps in the iPad app, so buttons and cards respond again.

title: Open a worker's dev server from your phone with /proxy/<port>/
description: Links like /proxy/3000/ on your amux address now open the dev server a worker started on that port, from any of your devices. If the server only listens on 127.0.0.1, amux shows a page naming the fix (--host 0.0.0.0) instead of a dead link. Owner only.

title: One switch turns the task board on or off for a worker
description: A worker can run without the shared board. Switch it off for a lane that only takes direct instructions; every other worker keeps its board.

title: amux requests lists what you asked for and whether it shipped
description: amux requests shows the owner's requests and whether each one has reached main, so you can see at a glance what is done and what is still open.

title: Mac-cleanup health tick runs under set -e, as the harness guard requires
description: The mac-cleanup health tick script now runs under set -e so any failing health check exits immediately and is caught by the harness guard, matching the contract it documents.

title: Server reaps zombie child processes that nothing was waiting on
description: Fixed a zombie process accumulation where child processes spawned by the server were never waited on. The server now installs a SIGCHLD handler that reaps all completed child processes.

title: Owner @-mention lets a worker reach a specific worker, one way
description: An @-mention from an owner message now resolves the named worker and delivers the message directly to that session. Workers cannot send @-mentions themselves — this is owner-to-worker only, one-way.

title: Mac health tick checks the whole machine and fixes what is safe to fix
description: The scheduled Mac cleanup tick now runs a full machine health check (disk, memory, fseventsd, launchd agents, open file handles) and auto-fixes safe issues such as clearing temp files and reaping stale Claude session dirs.

title: Reset also collapses every expanded worker card
description: Clicking Reset in the dashboard now also collapses all expanded worker cards, returning the fleet view to its compact default layout.

title: Search reports index lag per searched session
description: The search API now returns index_lag_seconds per session alongside results, so callers know whether very recent events may not yet be indexed.

title: Full-text search indexes session messages, logs, and transcripts with FTS5
description: amux now ships FTS5 full-text search covering three sources: session messages (sent/received via the messaging API), terminal logs (tmux scrollback), and companion chat transcripts. Search from the dashboard with Cmd+K, filter by session and time range, jump to context in the peek panel, or query the REST API: GET /api/search?q=your-query.

title: Open groups accept input from any worker, one way
description: Groups can now be configured as open, allowing any worker to post a message to the group's channel. All group members receive it. One-way only — workers broadcast to the group, the group does not reply.

title: Cmd+C and Cmd+X no longer interrupt a worker while typing
description: Fixed a regression where Cmd+C and Cmd+X keyboard shortcuts in the dashboard send composer were intercepted and sent an interrupt signal to the active worker instead of copying/cutting the selected text.

title: Peek chip actions guard the chat-target lookup
description: Shortcut chip actions in the peek panel now guard the chat-target session lookup before firing, preventing a crash when a chip action was triggered while no chat session was focused.

title: Sidebar sections fold individually; the whole sidebar folds on wide screens
description: Each sidebar section (workers, board, messages) now has a collapse toggle. On wide-phone screens, the entire sidebar can be folded away to give the active session's output full-width view.

title: Chat tab in peek panel gets terminal shortcut chips and Send/Queue toggle
description: The Chat tab inside the session peek panel now includes the same shortcut chips available in the terminal view, plus the Send/Queue delivery toggle. Chip actions route to the session's chat context rather than its terminal.

title: Idle browser-routing CDP Chrome instances are reaped
description: Fixed a resource leak where CDP Chrome instances used for browser routing remained alive after their session ended. The reaper now detects idle instances and terminates them.

title: Read Aloud beside Copy on every chat reply, with Stop and one at a time
description: Every chat reply now has a Read Aloud button beside Copy. Tapping it reads the reply with the Web Speech API. Only one reply plays at a time — starting a new one stops the previous. A Stop button appears during playback.

title: Scheduler form saves close only the form that was open
description: Saving a scheduler entry closed every open scheduler form instead of just the one being edited. Now only the form that triggered the save is closed.

title: Split side panel nesting guards scoped to split side only
description: Nesting-prevention guards for the split side panel were applying to the main panel too, causing view-switching issues when navigating between a worker in split view and other views. Guards are now scoped to the split side panel only.

title: Chat status bar agent count shows the session switcher, not live work count
description: The agent count shown in the Chat tab status bar was displaying the number of agents actively doing work rather than the number available in the session switcher. These are different numbers when some agents are idle. The count now correctly reflects the switcher list.

title: Companion chat context names background work and touched cards
description: The companion chat context summary was not showing background work or cards touched by the agent during a turn. The context now names background work in progress and references board cards the agent read or updated, giving a more complete picture of what the agent has been doing.

title: Typing in a Chat tab no longer shows an invalid session name toast
description: Typing in the Chat tab input box was triggering a validation pass that produced a toast notification saying the session name was invalid. The validation was running against the wrong field. The toast no longer appears when typing a chat message.

title: Draw settings saves apply in click order
description: Rapid successive saves in the Draw settings panel could arrive out of order, leaving an earlier value applied. Saves now land in the order they were triggered.

title: Held email card shows the full draft body; Edit starts from it
description: The held-email approval card was showing a truncated preview of the draft rather than the full body. The Edit button was also starting from a blank compose window rather than the held draft. Both are fixed: the card shows the complete draft, and clicking Edit pre-fills the compose panel with it.

title: Memory toolbar wraps on mobile instead of scrolling the panel
description: The memory panel toolbar was overflowing horizontally on phone-sized screens and making the panel scroll sideways. The toolbar now wraps onto a second line on narrow screens.

title: Scoped memory and rules follow their worker through every edit
description: Memory entries and rules scoped to a specific worker were not reliably reaching that worker after the scope was edited. The scoping mechanism now tracks the worker correctly through renames and re-scoping operations.

title: Draw canvas pointer coordinates re-measured before each drag
description: The Draw canvas was reading pointer coordinates against a cached bounding rect that could be stale after the panel was scrolled or the window was resized. The bounding rect is now re-measured at the start of each drag operation.

title: Chat turn ends on the provider final result, not process exit
description: A chat turn was considered complete when the Claude Code process exited, which could be before the provider had sent its final streaming result. This caused the last message in some turns to be cut off. The turn now ends when the provider signals completion.

title: X on Waiting on you card permanently dismisses the ask after confirm
description: Clicking the X on a Waiting on you card was dismissing it from view but not marking the ask as resolved, so it would reappear on the next render. The X now shows a confirmation and, on confirm, permanently dismisses the ask.

title: Large audio and video play reliably on flaky mobile connections
description: Large audio and video files were stalling on mobile connections with intermittent packet loss. Playback progress is now tracked against actual playback events rather than readyState, so stalls are detected and recovery is attempted. Closing the media player now stops playback and releases resources.

title: Skill examples shown when a skill is expanded, inferred from its Markdown
description: Expanding a skill in the Skills tab now shows example invocations for that skill. amux infers these automatically by reading the skill's Markdown body — imperative sentences, numbered step verbs, and code block trigger descriptions are turned into clickable example phrases. You can also supply explicit examples by adding an ## Examples section to the skill body. Explicit examples take precedence over inferred ones; amux shows up to 5 total. A clipboard button copies any example to paste elsewhere.

title: Skill examples appear in the / dropdown across the whole dashboard
description: Type / in any steering bar — worker, Chat, or board card input — to open the command palette. Every skill now lists its inferred or explicit example invocations as clickable suggestions directly below its name. Click an example to send it as a prompt to the session. This makes skills discoverable without memorizing exact command names or reading skill bodies.

title: Calendar shows every Google Calendar, Google-Calendar visual style, mobile-first, refreshes every minute
description: The amux calendar tab now syncs every Google Calendar you own — not just the primary calendar. Each calendar keeps its color from Google. The week and day view grids use a Google-Calendar-style layout with time-block rendering, so events look the same whether you're viewing them in Google Calendar or in the amux dashboard. The view is mobile-first and fits any screen. The calendar feed now refreshes every minute automatically without requiring a page reload.

title: Google Calendar sync: all occurrences in a time window, calendar colors, your own RSVP status
description: The Google Calendar read is now windowed: amux fetches every occurrence of every event (including recurring events) within the current view's time window, not just the first instance. Each event shows the calendar color it has in Google. For events with an invite, amux shows your RSVP status (accepted, tentative, declined) directly on the event block.

title: Connectors: Forget button confirms in-modal before removing credentials
description: The Forget button in the connector detail modal previously removed credentials immediately without asking for confirmation. It now shows an in-modal confirmation step before removing. The modal also confirms that the credentials were actually removed before it closes, so you can be confident the connector is fully disconnected.

title: Connectors: Test saves the health result back to the panel without a refresh
description: After clicking Test on a connector in the dashboard, the health status previously showed stale data until you left and returned to the panel. The connector health state is now saved back immediately after a browser-side Test, so the panel reflects the current health without requiring a reload.

title: Multiplayer typing, vault logins, password connections, browser fixes for headless hosts
description: Typing indicators in the send composer show when another dashboard client is composing. Vault-scoped login credentials work for password-protected connections. Browser sessions on headless hosts no longer fail with missing display errors.

title: Peek live frame cut at transcript end, not at quoted lines
description: The peek overlay's live frame now ends where the transcript ends rather than at the last quoted line, so the live view no longer drops content that appears after an agent quotes its own previous output.

title: Board writer unblocked; orphaned verifications resume automatically
description: A frozen PATCH that left the board writer wedged now self-heals: orphaned verification tasks resume, and the dashboard reports exactly which card froze the write and why.

title: File shortcuts are now scoped: global, group, or worker — all server-side
description: Keyboard shortcuts in the Files panel are now stored server-side at three scopes: global (every session), group (workers sharing a group), or individual worker. Shortcuts no longer reset on browser refresh and are shared across all dashboard clients for the same session.

title: Contract rule 4: each rule-4 lane launches in its own isolated worktree
description: Workers operating under contract rule 4 now automatically get their own git worktree, preventing shared-checkout race conditions between parallel agents working on the same repository.

title: Dashboard stays connected when the server rebuilds
description: The server now keeps port 8824 open across a binary rebuild, so the dashboard and iOS app stay connected instead of showing a disconnected banner every time a new version deploys. The old behavior closed the port for the gap between the old process dying and the new one binding, which caused brief disconnects on every commit. The port stays bound via a socket-passing mechanism so no client sees the swap.

title: CLI heals a stale AMUX_URL back to the live endpoint automatically
description: When AMUX_URL or AMUX_API points at a localhost address that is no longer responding, the CLI now reads the canonical URL from ~/.amux/endpoint.json and retries the request there. Previously, a session that had exported an old port number (e.g. from a shell that predated the last server restart) would silently fail or report connection refused with no guidance. The heal is transparent: one retry against the live endpoint, no user action required.

title: Faster steering delivery and attributable sender stamps on worker messages
description: Steering messages now arrive at idle sessions faster — the delivery path no longer waits for the session-status poll interval before injecting the message. Worker cards no longer generate churn on the shared board when multiple sessions are active: status updates that carry no new information are suppressed at the write layer rather than written and immediately overwritten. Sender attribution on peer messages now uses the server-stamped origin rather than a body-text heuristic, so a relayed message shows its true author in the board log.

title: Auto-approve: scoped per-ask policies for unattended agent runs
description: Agents can now run overnight without pausing for permission. A scoped owner policy auto-approves new asks by category — sign-in, key, and grant requests route back to the worker queue rather than surfacing to the owner. AMUX-5301.

title: CUA computer-use sandboxes: rung 3 of the browser access ladder
description: Agents now have a third browser rung: CUA (github.com/trycua/cua) sandboxed desktop for native apps, OS dialogs, and anything a headless browser cannot reach. Rung 1 (amux browser) and rung 2 (Chrome CDP) are tried first; CUA is the fallback. AMUX-5300.

title: Scoped browser profiles: restrict which agents access which saved logins
description: Browser auth profiles can now be scoped per-session, per-group, or globally. A worker for project A cannot read credentials saved for project B. AMUX-5307.

title: Chrome CDP profile sync: save real Chrome logins into amux profiles
description: Run profile-sync.mjs once to copy saved credentials from your real Chrome into amux browser profiles. Agents can then authenticate to sites without manual credential entry.

title: Cleanup: reap idle detached worktree scratch checkouts automatically
description: Detached worktree scratch checkouts that have been idle are now reaped automatically. MO-3631/3633.

title: Fix: collapsible tool and message headers can be highlighted
description: The collapsible tool-call and message headers in the peek panel now support text selection and highlight.

title: Standing approvals: pre-approve agent actions by category
description: Define standing approval rules in Settings > Approvals and amux will automatically answer matching agent escalations during overnight and unattended runs. Rules are scoped by category (access, credential, budget, production data, external outbound), support per-day caps and dollar-amount limits, and can be scoped to a specific worker, group, or fleet-wide. Every use is logged in a usage feed so you can review what was auto-approved after a run. Agents that hit a request outside your defined rules still surface to you as normal.

title: Goal keeper: the harness re-prompts agents until a goal is met
description: Set a goal for a worker session using the /goal command and the amux harness will automatically continue the session if the goal is not met when the agent stops. For example, '/goal all tests pass' keeps the agent working through failures until the test suite is green, rather than stopping at the first green run. The goal keeper handles premature exits, context overflows, and intermediate stops without any manual intervention.

title: Chat workers work offline with message queuing
description: Chat workers (the conversational agent type alongside coding workers) now support offline operation with a persistent message queue. Messages sent to a chat worker while it is offline are queued and delivered when it reconnects, matching the offline behavior of coding workers. Combined with live streaming (turns render incrementally as they arrive) and turn retry (an interrupted turn can be re-sent without retyping), chat workers are now reliable for long-running asynchronous tasks.

title: Collapsible tool-call blocks in the peek view
description: Tool-call output blocks in the session peek view are now collapsible. Long bash output, file reads, and multi-step tool sequences fold to a one-line summary and expand on click. This makes it significantly easier to scan an agent's recent turns without scrolling through hundreds of lines of command output — the decision-making turns are visible at a glance while details are one click away.

title: Workers-per-row layout override in Settings > Device
description: A new device-level setting lets you override the automatic workers-per-row calculation in the dashboard grid. Set it to 1 on a phone for a single-column view, or push it to 4 on a wide monitor to pack more sessions onto one screen. The setting is per-device (stored locally) and does not affect other viewers of the same dashboard.

title: Stalled builder is automatically kickstarted instead of just reported
description: When the amux auto-builder stalls without producing a new binary (detected by comparing the last build timestamp against recent commits), the runtime job now sends a kickstart signal instead of only logging a warning. This prevents the silent build-lag issue where a commit was pushed, the builder was stuck, and the server kept serving the old binary with no user-visible indication that anything was wrong.

title: Pinned notes: floating macOS overlays from the dashboard
description: A new Pinned tab in the dashboard lets you push any text note to a floating macOS window that stays on top of every other application. The overlay uses a frosted-glass effect, is always-on-top, and can be dismissed or repositioned without leaving the dashboard. Useful for keeping acceptance criteria, sprint context, or agent instructions visible while working in other apps. Controlled via the 'amux pin' CLI command and the POST /api/pinned endpoint.

title: Claude workers started through the server get a session identity
description: Workers launched via 'amux start' now go through the server's session-start path, which stamps the AMUX_SESSION environment variable and registers the session in the database before the Claude process starts. Previously, directly launched workers had no session identity until their first check-in, which caused attribution gaps in the board and message history during the first few turns.

title: Idle re-prompt when a lane promised a next step (AMUX-5236)
description: When a session's turn ends with a message like 'I'll add tests next' or 'I'll commit this shortly' and the session then goes idle without acting, amux now re-prompts it once with the outstanding commitment. This prevents the common failure mode where an agent announces a follow-up step, context closes, and the step never happens. The re-prompt fires at the next idle detection cycle and is rate-limited to once per commitment to avoid loops.

title: Shell scheduler runs now store exit code and output tail (AMUX-5241)
description: Schedule runs with kind=shell now persist the process exit code and a noise-filtered tail of stdout/stderr in the run record. The tail is deduped and truncated to the last 20 meaningful lines (blank lines, repeated separators, and progress bars filtered out). Exit codes are visible in GET /api/schedules/runs and in the dashboard Scheduler tab — a failed shell run now shows the actual error rather than just 'non-zero exit'.

title: Prompts typed directly into a pane are recorded in Messages
description: Text entered directly into a tmux pane by the owner (outside the dashboard's message input) is now captured and stored as a Messages row attributed to the owner. Previously, only messages sent via the API or dashboard were recorded; direct pane input was invisible to the message history, search, and the per-session message count in the sessions view.

title: Resume fallback triggers only when --resume fails immediately
description: The 'amux start' CLI previously fell back to starting a new conversation whenever --resume returned a non-zero exit, including mid-run failures that had nothing to do with the resume attempt itself. The fallback now fires only when --resume fails on the first invocation with no prior output, ensuring that a crash during an established run does not silently discard context by starting fresh.

title: Browser automation: grounded observe → act → verify loop
description: GET /api/browser/state now returns an observation_id and structured element metadata (ref, role, accessible name, frame path, bounding rect, disabled/checked state) for every interactive element including same-origin iframes and shadow DOM. POST /api/browser/action click accepts ref + observation_id and refuses stale documents, disabled elements, and obscured targets. Every action reports an observed_effect (navigated, url_changed, dom_mutations counted, none_observed) so agents can verify their actions actually worked. An optional expect field polls for a specific post-action condition before returning. Replaces the older index-based clicking that could silently act on the wrong element after a page rerender.

title: Board tab can be hidden from the dashboard
description: The Board tab in the amux dashboard can now be toggled off via the worker tab customizer. Useful for sessions or setups where the kanban view is not relevant and a cleaner interface is preferred.

title: Host pressure guard: automation backs off under load
description: amux now monitors host CPU and memory pressure levels. When pressure crosses a threshold, the automation layer backs off from spawning new browser instances and renices runaway processes rather than letting them consume the machine. Overnight agent runs on shared or resource-constrained hardware are significantly more stable. The pressure level is visible in GET /api/health.

title: Workers wake automatically when their commits go live
description: amux now detects when a new build goes live by polling its own health endpoint and comparing the running commit hash. When the hash advances, it identifies which worker sessions authored commits in the deployed range (via the Amux-Session git trailer) and sends each one a wake message. Workers resume automatically with deploy context and can run smoke tests or verify their changes without any manual follow-up.

title: Named clearance signals for cross-agent coordination
description: Board cards can now wait on a named signal with amux signal wait <CARD> <name>, and any lane can raise the signal with amux signal raise <name> --note <text>. When a signal is raised, every card waiting on that name wakes automatically. Replaces polling loops and manual check-ins for cross-agent dependencies — the waiting session resumes as soon as the dependency clears.

title: Outbound email approvals stay pending until resolved
description: Outbound email approval requests now remain in a pending state until explicitly approved or rejected, rather than expiring silently. Repeated requests for the same email are deduplicated rather than stacked. A daily digest of pending approvals is delivered so nothing falls through the gaps.

title: Email inbox paginates past the 500-message cap
description: GET /api/email/inbox now supports a cursor parameter and paginates through inboxes with more than 500 messages. Previously the endpoint silently returned only the most recent 500, with no indication that messages were missing.

title: Scheduler reclaims memory when amux is under pressure
description: On macOS, the scheduler now monitors amux's own memory footprint and triggers a compaction pass when it exceeds the configured threshold. Keeps the server running cleanly on machines where agent fleets accumulate state over long overnight runs.

title: Composer recovers chunked uploads across reloads
description: Chunked file uploads from the mobile composer are now persisted in IndexedDB and recovered automatically if the page reloads mid-upload. Previously a reload would silently discard the in-progress upload with no recovery path.

title: Typed needsyou asks are exempt from age-based auto-discard
description: Cards created via a typed needsyou ask (question + unblocking sentence) are now flagged as owner-gated and excluded from the board hygiene job's age-based auto-discard pass. A card that is genuinely waiting on a decision should not be discarded for being old.

title: Dashboard sends messages directly, queues only on failure
description: Message sends from the web dashboard now go directly over SSE. The local queue is used only as a fallback when the direct path fails, rather than as the default path. Reduces latency and eliminates the double-delivery edge case when a queued message also arrived via SSE.

title: amux board shepherd: escape hatch for stuck cards
description: New command: amux board shepherd. Scans for cards in invalid states (doing with no active session, blocked by a session that no longer exists, done without evidence on a gated card) and offers targeted fixes. Replaces the previous approach of manual state inspection and curl patches.

title: Mobile terminal renders diffs and streams incrementally
description: The mobile dashboard now renders terminal output as incremental diffs rather than full-frame snapshots. Output appears as it arrives, so monitoring an overnight agent from your phone shows live progress. Fixes AF-640.

title: Terminal scroll notices kept truthful
description: Fixed scroll position notices in the terminal view that could report stale state, making the indicator mislead about whether output had advanced since the last view.

title: Board deduplicates autofix cards and expires stale alerts
description: Autofix cards that trigger repeatedly for the same condition are now deduplicated rather than accumulating. Stale alert cards past their TTL are expired automatically. Conversational acks (messages that only acknowledge a prior message) are filtered out of the capture queue.

title: Board hygiene runtime job: needsyou aging and stale card sweeps
description: A new background job runs continuously to keep the board clean. It ages out stale needsyou cards (no activity past a configurable threshold), deduplicates autofix alert bursts, and removes conversational acks that clog the review queue. Morning review queues now surface real decisions rather than resolved notifications.

title: Break worker-list overload loop on session boot
description: Fixed an overload loop that could fire repeatedly during worker list initialization when a session booted while many sessions were active.

title: Session log rotation, audit dir cleanup, and age-pruned dirs
description: Added log rotation for session log files to prevent unbounded growth. Audit directories are cleaned when their associated sessions are gone. Additional directories are now included in age-based pruning.

title: Board captures require a disposition before requeuing
description: Fixed a gap where a captured message could be requeued without a recorded disposition, leaving the audit trail incomplete. The board now requires an explicit outcome (fold, discard, or forward) before the capture is released back to the queue.

title: Lanes can declare a card fold directly from the CLI
description: Previously, a card fold required constructing a hand-rolled log entry. Now any lane can declare a fold with a single CLI command: amux board fold <card-id> --into <target-id>. The server records it identically to a system-generated fold, so the audit trail is consistent regardless of how the fold happened. Useful when a task absorbs another mid-sprint and the board should reflect that without manual cleanup.

title: Workspace members can be assigned to scoped teams
description: Engineering organizations using amux can now partition their workspace into named teams. Each team has its own scoped membership, so a mobile team and a backend team can share one amux instance while seeing only their own sessions, board cards, and logs. Team assignment is managed through the Settings tab.

title: Worker message view now has composable filters
description: The worker message panel now supports composable filters: filter by session name, runtime type, or message keyword in any combination. Previously you had to scroll through all messages across all workers to find what you were looking for. With composable filters, watching 10 mixed Claude Code and Codex CLI sessions simultaneously is manageable at a glance. (AMUX-4242)

title: Owner access link is now visible in Settings
description: The dashboard Settings tab now shows the owner access link directly, so you can copy it without running a CLI command. Previously, finding the access URL required running amux url or checking server.env. This is especially useful when setting up remote access from a new device.

title: Server logs can be filtered by IP address
description: The log analysis endpoint now accepts an IP filter. Pass ?ip=192.168.1.x to isolate requests from a specific client. Previously, the only way to narrow down log noise from a shared amux instance was to grep the raw log file. The filter is now a first-class query parameter with proper column indexing.

title: Repeated card re-assignment to the same lane is now flagged
description: If a lane is handed the same board card more than once in a short window, the invariants panel now surfaces this as a violation. The silent looping pattern — where a session fails a card and it bounces back repeatedly — was previously invisible until you dug through logs. Now it appears in the dashboard health view as soon as it starts. (AF-543)

title: Board idle dispatch no longer loops when no cards are available
description: Fixed a bug where the idle card dispatch and recovery loop ran continuously when the board had no todo cards, burning CPU and producing noisy logs. The scheduler now backs off properly when there is nothing to claim rather than spinning. (AMUX-4168)

title: Email ledger shows send status on every row
description: The email audit log now shows whether each message was sent successfully, failed, or is pending directly on every row. Previously you had to click into a message to find its delivery status — unhelpful for scanning a day's outbound volume at a glance.

title: Email approval status is readable without triggering the approval flow
description: You can now see whether a pending email was approved, rejected, or timed out without going through the approval interaction. Previously, checking the status required presenting the approval prompt, which consumed an interaction slot even when you just wanted to audit the outcome.

title: AI provider catalog is now typed and centralized
description: All AI providers — Claude, GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex — are now defined in a single typed catalog shared across the server. Adding a new provider or model variant no longer requires changes across multiple files. This makes multi-runtime fleet configuration more reliable and reduces the surface area for provider name mismatches.

title: Tab customizer button now works on phones
description: The tab customizer button was clipped off-screen on every phone, making it impossible to rearrange or hide tabs from a mobile device. The button is now fully visible and tappable on all phone sizes. Manage your dashboard view from your phone just as you would from a desktop.

title: Board drain trigger no longer loops forever when verification time is missing
description: A board trigger with no verification time set would re-drain the same card in a silent loop, sending duplicate task prompts to sessions. The drain now correctly waits for a verification window before re-triggering. This affected any auto-drain setup where the trigger condition was satisfied but verification hadn't been configured.

title: Board API now tells you exactly which fields an unrecognized trigger key expected
description: When you POST a board trigger with an unrecognized key, the API now names the correct field names you should have used, instead of silently ignoring the key. This makes it faster to debug automation scripts and integrations that send slightly wrong field names.

title: Board list loads descriptions faster — 512-char prefix hydrated immediately
description: The board list now hydrates the first 512 characters of each card description on initial load, so you can read card context without opening individual cards. Previously the list returned only titles and metadata. The change is backwards-compatible and requires no client-side update.

title: Board auto-drain: idle workers now automatically claim the next backlog task
description: Sessions that finish their queue can now opt in to automatically claiming the next open card from the shared board backlog. When a session declines to drain, amux logs the reason, so you can see exactly why an agent went idle rather than picking up new work. Enable per-session or fleet-wide via Settings. Pairs with the autonomous work lifecycle to create a fully self-managing team.

title: Telegram groups: @-mention your lane in a group to steer it, like a private chat
description: Link any Telegram group to a session that already has a private Telegram link. Messages in the group reach the session only when they @-mention the lane name, so the bot stays silent by default. Linking a group requires an existing private link as proof of ownership. Replies flow back into the group thread, so your whole team can follow along.

title: Autonomous work lifecycle: tasks spawned from board cards now run to completion
description: Tasks created from captured board commands now travel through a full plan-execute-verify lifecycle instead of stopping after the first tool call. Worker status and task context stay consistent across the whole lifecycle. Scheduler health checks catch stuck loops before they consume tokens.

title: Browser start returns 409 when the profile is already in use by another session
description: Starting the browser against a profile already held by another session now returns 409 Conflict with the active session named in the error body, rather than a generic 502. Callers can distinguish a busy profile from a genuine failure and surface the right message to the user.

title: Telegram bot connector: steer agents and get alerts on your phone via Telegram
description: amux now has a built-in Telegram connector. Create a bot via BotFather, add the token to server.env, and link a chat with /start. The server relays agent terminal output to Telegram automatically, including fenced code blocks, links, and formatted markdown. Use @lane mentions in Telegram to route your replies to a specific running agent. Overnight agents that hit a stalled prompt can now reach you on your phone — you reply, they continue.

title: Fleet-wide cross-group messaging now has a single global default in Settings
description: A new global setting lets you allow or deny cross-group agent messaging for the entire fleet in one place. Previously, enabling cross-group sends required approving each message. The new default applies fleet-wide and can be overridden per group or per worker. Combined with the worker-level Spans groups toggle, you can configure the right isolation level for each part of your fleet without per-message approval prompts.

title: Worker cards now have a Spans groups toggle for cross-group messaging
description: Each worker card in the dashboard now has a Spans groups menu item. Toggling it on lets that specific worker send to and receive from workers in any group, without a per-message approval. Useful for coordinator agents that need to route tasks across the fleet, while keeping the rest of the fleet group-isolated for security and billing accountability.

title: Cross-group allowances now resolve worker before group before global
description: Cross-group messaging allowances follow the same resolution order as credentials: worker setting overrides group setting, group setting overrides the global default. This means you can set a conservative global default (deny) and open specific workers or groups without touching anything else. No more per-message approval dialogs for agents you have already explicitly allowed.

title: Review requests now route to the reviewer, fire at the right moment, and explain why they're stale
description: Three fixes to the board review-request flow landed together. Review requests now go to the designated reviewer rather than only the owner. They fire when a card enters review state, not just when a note is added. And a stale request now explains its own staleness instead of being silently droppable — so reviewers understand the context without having to dig through the card history.

title: Blocked tasks now surface as their own dimension across the fleet
description: The board now tracks a blocked dimension separately from status. Any card can be marked blocked-on another card — the dashboard shows blocked tasks at a glance across your whole fleet, and the GET /api/board/ready endpoint excludes them so agents only pull work they can actually start. Existing cards are not rewritten: the new dimension appears only when you explicitly set a blocked-on relationship. Pairs with the dependency graph shipped alongside it.

title: GET /api/board/ready surfaces only the tasks an agent can start right now
description: A new endpoint returns only board cards that are in todo status and have no incomplete dependencies.
