Agents that self-schedule by polling the board can now pull from /api/board/ready and be guaranteed they will never start a task whose prerequisite is still in progress. Combine with blocked-on to build a full dependency graph — the ready endpoint is the read side that makes it actionable.

title: Board cards now carry a continuation contract so any agent can resume a crashed peer's work
description: A claimed card can now record a continuation — what the working agent was doing, which files it had touched, and what the next step is. If the agent crashes or its context is exhausted, the card retains this state. The next agent to pick up the card reads the continuation and resumes at the same point rather than starting over. This makes the fleet resilient to mid-task failures without requiring human intervention.

title: Every board card now records when it entered its current state — so time-in-state is computable
description: The entered_state_at field now stamps every status transition with the time it occurred. This makes it possible to compute how long any task has been in todo, doing, review, or done — directly from the board API without consulting git history. The dashboard uses this to surface tasks that have been doing unusually long, which is often the signal that an agent is stuck.

title: GPT-5.6 Sol is now available in the Codex model picker
description: GPT-5.6 Sol appears in the dashboard's Codex model list. Select it when registering or reconfiguring a Codex session. The model is available wherever Codex CLI is supported — see the Claude Code vs Codex vs Gemini CLI guide for a runtime comparison.

title: Board nudges can now be toggled at global, group, or per-worker scope
description: You can now enable or disable board nudges at three levels: globally for the whole fleet, per group, or per individual worker. Previously nudges were all-or-nothing. This lets busy workers turn off nudges while active and quieter ones keep them on — without affecting the rest of the fleet.

title: amux refuses to start new agents when your server is running low on memory
description: Before admitting each new worker, amux now checks available memory headroom on the host. If RAM is critically low, the new session is refused and the reason surfaces in the dashboard and via GET /api/health/invariants. Existing agents keep running — only new session creation is blocked until memory frees up. No configuration required. Prevents the 3am OOM cascade where starting too many agents all at once swaps every process to disk.

title: The auto-compact toggle now shows the memory threshold that actually fires it
description: The auto-compact toggle in the dashboard was displaying a description that didn't match the real compaction threshold in effect. The setting now accurately states the percentage-of-context-used threshold it's configured to fire at. If you set a custom threshold via AMUX_AUTO_COMPACT_THRESHOLD, the toggle reflects that value rather than a hardcoded display.

title: Peeking a worker's output now reaches the live fleet lane, not just the database record
description: GET /api/workers/{name}/peek was reading the database row rather than querying the live tmux session, so you could get stale output for an actively-running worker. The endpoint now resolves to the fleet lane and reads current terminal output. If you use peek from scripts or CI to monitor active agents, this gives you accurate real-time data.

title: Create an isolated worker with no harness tools injected
description: A new ISOLATED option in the session create dialog strips all amux harness tools from the worker at creation time. Use it when you want to run a tool — Plandex, a custom CLI, or a raw Claude Code session — inside amux's monitoring layer without amux's own steering instructions interfering. The dialog also now scrolls to reach the option on small screens.

title: amux-worker: cross-CLI amux API client for any terminal
description: amux-worker is a new cross-CLI API client that lets any terminal — one without a local amux install — make fleet calls against a remote amux server. Point it at AMUX_URL and your auth token to read the board, send messages to workers, peek at session output, and manage the fleet from scripts or CI pipelines. Phase 0/MVP of the amux skills system.

title: Creating a Claude session no longer accidentally targets a Gemini worker
description: The create-session dialog's model default could land on a Gemini worker configuration even when Claude was selected, silently routing the new session to the wrong runtime. The default now resolves to a Claude worker correctly. If you saw new sessions starting with unexpected model behavior, this is the fix.

title: Real-time backbone health is now visible in the dashboard
description: The SSE realtime backbone now publishes a joined health signal — server-side connection count meets the client-side reconnect beacon count. The dashboard can now show whether your fleet is truly live-connected or silently polling. A near-zero stale reconnect count shortly after a deploy is expected (ramp-up); the live connections metric is the discriminator. Check GET /api/debug/sse for the full breakdown.

title: Every fleet gh call now uses your GitHub App token automatically
description: A token shim now sits in front of every `gh` CLI call made by an agent in the fleet. When a GitHub App is configured in amux, its installation token is injected automatically — no per-session credential setup, no agent-by-agent authentication. Teams using GitHub Apps for CI, PR creation, or repository access get fleet-wide coverage without touching each worker's environment.

title: Board pickup scoring now weights by task age — older tasks surface first
description: The board drive previously picked up todo items in pos-LIFO order, which meant tasks added early could be buried under newer ones indefinitely. Age-weighted pickup scoring now blends position with how long a card has been waiting. Tasks that have sat in todo for hours or days score higher and get claimed sooner, keeping the backlog moving rather than stacking.

title: Duplicate / clone any live session
description: Any running session can now be duplicated with one API call (POST /api/sessions/<name>/clone) or via the dashboard 'Duplicate' button. The twin is registered alongside the original, inherits its project config and board association, and is immediately ready to receive messages. Use it to run parallel prompt experiments, split a long task across two agents, or A/B test two implementation approaches simultaneously without re-queuing from scratch.

title: Archived cards collapse into a drawer on the board
description: The board's Archived section now folds behind a collapsible 'Archived (N)' header by default. On boards with dozens of completed cards, this keeps the active columns scannable without discarding history. Click the header to expand it when you need to review or restore an archived card.

title: Discard a held email draft and dismiss the approvals banner
description: The email composition flow now includes a Discard button for held drafts and a way to collapse the approvals banner once you've decided not to send. Previously, a draft that was no longer relevant stayed in the approval queue with no way to remove it short of sending it or leaving it indefinitely. The banner now auto-collapses after a discard.

title: amux reserves 30% of the plan window for the human operator
description: Under heavy overnight fleet load, the agent pool could consume the full API plan window, leaving no budget for the human operator's own interactive sessions the next morning. amux now reserves 30% of the plan window for human use and constrains agent activity to the remaining 70%. If the fleet reaches the ceiling it queues new work rather than continuing to consume — the reservation is enforced, not advisory.

title: Send to a specific worker by its ID
description: The worker-send route is now canonical: POST /api/sessions/<worker-name>/send is a stable, documented endpoint that external systems can address directly. Previously the send path had to be discovered from the session listing on each call. This change makes it practical to wire GitHub Actions, webhooks, and other external triggers to a named worker by ID, since the URL is now stable across restarts and server updates.

title: Schedules show estimated turns per day at creation and on edit
description: When you create or edit a recurring schedule, amux now calculates and displays the estimated agent turns per day that schedule will consume based on its cadence. A schedule running every hour shows 24 turns/day; one running every weekday at 9am shows 5. This lets you forecast token spend before committing to a schedule, rather than discovering cost only after the first week of runs.

title: Messages hold during rate limits instead of being dropped
description: When a message is sent to a session that is currently rate-limited — either by API quota or by Claude Code's own rate limit — amux now holds the message in a delivery queue and delivers it as soon as the limit is released. Previously the message was silently dropped, with no indication to the sender that it had not been received. This affects agent-to-agent pipelines and external API callers who cannot predict whether a target worker is rate-limited at send time.

title: Board tasks now record when they closed
description: Every board card now stores a closed_at timestamp the moment its status moves to done or verified. This makes sprint analytics queryable without exporting: you can ask 'what did each agent close this week?' and get a precise answer rather than inferring closure from activity logs.

title: Board audit trail: which permission layer allowed each transition
description: Board status transitions now record which permission layer approved the move — agent-auto, human-review, or force-override — alongside the actor and timestamp. Engineering managers and team leads can audit the board history and know not just what changed but under which authorization. No additional configuration required.

title: CLI no longer hangs when the server is unreachable
description: Previously, running an amux CLI command against a server that was down or unreachable would hang indefinitely — the shell prompt never returned until you killed the process. The CLI now detects a failed connection immediately, prints a clear error with the server address and how to restart it, and exits with a non-zero status. Scripts and CI jobs that call amux commands will no longer stall silently on a down server.

title: Inbox loads 4x faster with Gmail batch API
description: The Gmail inbox now fetches all message metadata in a single batch request rather than one API call per message. Inbox loads with 480 messages now complete in roughly 5 round-trips instead of 480, cutting load time by 4x. The change is transparent — the inbox, thread, and search views work identically.

title: @-mention any worker in the scheduler command editor
description: The @-worker autocomplete dropdown — previously limited to the message composer — now attaches to any text input, starting with the scheduler command editor. Type @ in a scheduled command to pick a session name from a live fleet list. The correct session name gets inserted without typos, which matters for scheduled commands that run unattended.

title: Board progress note notifies the card owner
description: When a peer session adds a progress note to a board card you own, the card owner now receives a live notification and the success line names the recipient. Previously a progress note was written silently — the card owner had no way to know a peer had updated their card without polling the board. Works across all running sessions in the same fleet.

title: Weekly disk watchdog warns before caches fill your drive
description: amux now runs a weekly disk watchdog that scans for directories consuming more than configurable thresholds and emits a warning before writes start failing. Particularly useful for teams running amux on a shared server with heavy multi-session usage — Rust build caches, log archives, and tmux scrollback can accumulate several gigabytes per week without notice.

title: Server updates apply in place — no restart window
description: The amux Rust server now self-adopts new builds in place: when the auto-builder detects a new commit touching the server crate, it installs the updated binary and the running process exits cleanly for launchd to relaunch immediately. Sessions keep running through the changeover. Previously, applying a server update required a manual restart and introduced a brief window where the server was unavailable.

title: Pane-churn — model-agnostic generation signal for any AI agent
description: amux can now detect when any AI coding agent is actively generating output — not just Claude Code. The pane-churn signal watches for rapid terminal output change and infers a 'working' status regardless of which model or runtime is running (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider, or a custom script). Previously, working-state detection relied on Claude Code-specific UI patterns. Pane-churn works universally.

title: Status-explain — see exactly how amux derived a session's current state
description: Each session status chip in the dashboard now carries an explanation tooltip showing exactly how amux derived that state — which signal won, what it saw in the pane, and why it chose that status over alternatives. Previously a session that showed 'idle' or 'working' gave no indication of the reasoning behind the label. Status-explain makes the derivation transparent, so you can trust the status or understand why it's wrong.

title: Live canary per connector service — ok / api_error / unreachable / not_granted
description: Each service in the Connectors tab now shows a live health indicator — ok, api_error, unreachable, or not_granted — updated in real time by a background canary probe. If a credential stops working (expired token, revoked key, wrong scope), the connector shows api_error or not_granted immediately, and amux creates an autofix card on the board naming the affected service. Dashboard status dots reflect connector health so you can see at a glance whether your agent fleet has the credentials it needs.

title: OAuth broker — authorize once, every agent shares the grant
description: The new OAuth broker lets you authorize an external service (Google, GitHub, or any OAuth 2.0 provider) a single time and share that grant across every agent in your fleet. Previously each session that needed an OAuth-protected API had to either hold its own token or go through a separate auth flow. Now the broker holds the grant centrally, mints short-lived tokens on demand, and injects them as environment variables at session launch. Tokens stay out of CLAUDE.md and git history.

title: Files view sorts by last modified (newest first) by default
description: The Files tab now opens with files sorted by last-modified time, newest first — the file you just wrote or edited is at the top. Previously the default sort was alphabetical, which buried the most recently changed files in the middle of long directory listings. The sort preference is persisted per-session so it stays across page refreshes.

title: PWA resume lands on your exact last location — peek tab and closed state included
description: Reopening the amux PWA (or reloading the dashboard) now returns you to exactly where you left off — the same session selected, the same peek panel open (or closed), and the same tab active inside the peek. Previously reopening the app always landed on the sessions list with no peek open, requiring several taps to get back to the session you were monitoring. The restored state includes which peeks were explicitly closed, so a closed peek stays closed rather than reopening on resume.

title: Email read-back shows your sent copy, not Gmail's rewritten version
description: When you read back a message you just sent via /api/email/message/<id>, you now see the exact content you sent — not the Gmail-rewritten delivered copy, which could strip formatting or alter structure. Affects outbound read-back for all Gmail-connected accounts. Useful for confirming exactly what your agent sent before acting on the reply.

title: Browser automation start echoes ignored fields and accepts a viewport parameter
description: POST /api/browser/start now returns an ignored_fields list when you pass unrecognized parameters, so a wrong guess reads as a debugging hint rather than a silent no-op. Also adds a viewport parameter ({width, height}) so you can set screen dimensions at launch — useful for responsive layout testing and screenshots at specific breakpoints.

title: Email reply audit rows now carry to/subject fields like send rows
description: The email send audit log (GET /api/email/log) previously showed blank to and subject fields for replies — only direct sends were fully attributed. Reply rows now carry the recipient and subject thread, so the audit trail is consistent whether your agent sent a fresh email or replied in a thread.

title: BM25 board search — full-text relevance ranking with match highlighting
description: The board search bar now uses BM25 relevance ranking across every card field — title, description, notes, session tags, and status — with match highlighting on results. Previously the board used substring filtering with no ranking, so a query matching dozens of cards returned them in arbitrary order. BM25 brings TF-IDF style scoring so the most relevant cards surface first. Particularly useful when running large fleets where a session might have hundreds of past cards.

title: Email file attachments — attach PDFs, CSVs, and files to /send and /reply
description: Both /api/email/send and /api/email/reply now accept an attachments array. Each entry takes a filename, base64-encoded content, and MIME type. The email is sent as multipart/mixed so the body and attachment arrive together in Gmail. Agents can generate a report, export a CSV, or produce a PDF and email it to a recipient without any manual step. Works with all connected Gmail accounts.

title: Email attachment inline flag and download endpoint
description: Attachments sent via /api/email/send or /api/email/reply are now flagged as inline or attachment in the MIME structure. A new GET /api/email/attachment/<id> download endpoint returns the raw attachment bytes, useful for agents or operators who need to retrieve a previously sent file. This closes the loop on the attachment workflow: send, confirm arrival, and retrieve if needed.

title: Session status: API 5xx / Overloaded — distinct state when provider is rate-limited or down
description: Sessions can now report an Overloaded status when the AI provider is returning 5xx errors or explicit rate-limit responses. Previously these events caused sessions to appear as crashed or stalled with no distinct visual signal. The new status surfaces in the dashboard session card, the iOS app status chip, and the API response, so operators can distinguish 'agent is broken' from 'provider is temporarily unavailable' without reading terminal output.

title: CLI warns once when $AMUX_URL points to the dead port
description: If $AMUX_URL still points to the retired 8822 port, the CLI now prints one warning per session and exits 1 rather than silently returning empty JSON. Sessions started before the port migration get a clear signal — and the fix — instead of unexplained empty responses.

title: Push alerts report delivered only when an endpoint accepts
description: The alert endpoint previously reported 'sent' even when no configured push endpoint accepted the delivery. The response now accurately reflects whether at least one endpoint received the notification — no more false-green status on missed alerts.

title: EnvSpec apply — creates each worker's workdir on bootstrap
description: When applying an EnvSpec on a fresh machine, worker directories did not exist and the apply failed silently. apply now creates each worker's workdir before starting the session — bootstrap works out of the box on a clean install.

title: EnvSpec — save your entire AI team config, restore it anywhere
description: GET /api/envspec/export snapshots your live environment as a single portable YAML: workers with their prompts, schedules, board cards, file seeds, and environment variables. POST /api/envspec/apply recreates the entire team on any amux instance. Clone a working agent setup to a new machine, onboard teammates with the same fleet config, or snapshot a team state before a major change. The exporter and all five appliers (env vars, workers, schedules, cards, files) shipped together across commits e1b8c2a, 59bd282, ba8a0e0, 94b1c40.

title: Accountability sweep — sessions without active work get a nudge
description: Every 30 minutes amux identifies sessions that have been idle but hold no board card in doing. Those lanes receive an automated nudge prompting them to pick up a queued card or report their status. Keeps the fleet accountable without manual oversight — nothing silently idles while the board accumulates stale cards.

title: Board self-drives its backlog — stalled cards surface automatically
description: The board now nudges the owning session when a todo card has sat without movement past its type's SLA. Instead of a growing backlog that silently rots, cards announce themselves: the session receives a notice naming the stalled card and its waiting time. The board drives itself rather than relying on manual review.

title: Copyable message ID on every message row
description: Every message row in the Messages tab now shows a copyable MSG-<id> badge, matching the style of schedule ID badges. Makes it easy to reference a specific message when routing work or debugging.

title: Cloud auto-deploys on green CI
description: When the CI pipeline passes on main, the cloud image and gateway deploy automatically. Only the final recreate step stays manual. Cuts the cloud release loop from a manual multi-step process to a single push.

title: Gmail mailbox — labels, inbox, thread view, and send
description: The Mail view now has a full mailbox UI: label sidebar, inbox list, thread view, and send panel. Backed by the Gmail API through the same connected accounts used for /api/email/send and /api/email/reply.

title: amux board needsyou actually moves the card
description: The 'amux board needsyou' command previously only tagged the card without changing its status. It now moves the card to the needsyou status as documented. Running it no longer silently leaves the card untouched.

title: Map tab — mind-map, Obsidian import, and fleet org chart
description: A new Map tab surfaces /api/graph as a mind-map of your fleet and board. Includes Obsidian vault import (nodes link to vault pages) and a fleet org chart view showing session groups and active lanes.

title: Settings key no longer wiped mid-typing
description: The async env refresh that fires when the Settings tab opens was overwriting the text field while a user was typing a new API key. The refresh no longer clobbers a field with a pending edit in progress.

title: Unified offline pending badge for uploads and recordings
description: The pending count badge now reflects both queued file uploads and queued dictation recordings in a single summary (e.g. '2 uploads + 1 recording queued (840 KB)'). Previously the two offline queues had separate, inconsistently styled indicators.

title: Cost tab — real-time token spend per session and across your fleet
description: The new /api/observability endpoint powers a Cost tab in the dashboard showing live token spend per session and total fleet burn. The ledger was previously inert — tokens read 0 because the write path was missing. Now every token consumed, including subagent delegation, is recorded and surfaced in real time.

title: Saved messages and habits — reuse prompts you send every day
description: Frequently used prompts can now be saved as habits and recalled from the message panel. The token-reset route that clears a session's spend counter is also live — previously missing, so the reset button silently did nothing.

title: Subagent token spend now charged to the delegating session
description: When a session delegates to a subagent, the subagent's token consumption is now recorded under the parent lane that spawned it. Previously subagent tokens were lost, not counted anywhere. Fleet cost totals are now accurate even for deeply orchestrated runs.

title: Board pickup is now reactive — agents claim the next card immediately on completion
description: Previously a session completing a card had to wait up to 30 seconds for the next pickup poll before claiming a new one. Now a status-change event triggers immediate re-evaluation. Useful for high-throughput overnight runs where idle time between tasks accumulates.

title: Backlog-triage nudge — sessions with 10+ stale cards get reminded
description: A session sitting on 10 or more cards that have not moved in over 24 hours now receives a triage nudge naming the stale count and suggesting review. Prevents backlog rot from silently accumulating across long-running fleets.

title: New Worker and Connect modals restored — 6 dead routes fixed
description: The New Worker and Connect modals were silently failing. Six API routes they depended on returned 404 after the Python-to-Rust migration, and the templates directory they referenced was gone. All 6 routes are restored. The Connect panel now shows a clear message when iTerm2's pane list is empty instead of blaming the user.

title: needsyou board status now surfaces — 23 of 38 blocked asks were invisible
description: Cards with status 'needsyou' were not surfaced in any board view, so sessions could file an ask for human input and it would disappear from sight. 23 of 38 open asks were in this state. The status now appears in the board and fleet summaries. A card filed into needsyou also carries its ask text so the owner sees what is needed without clicking through.

title: Board status-request and status-update routes fixed — were returning 405
description: POST /api/board/:id/status-request and /api/board/:id/status-update were returning 405. These are the two endpoints the whole fleet is told to use for D1-exit status reporting. Sessions following the documented instruction were hitting a dead end. Both routes are now mounted correctly.

title: Commit nudge — agents are reminded to commit before progress is lost
description: amux now detects when a worker has made meaningful progress — changed files, new output — without committing, and sends a nudge before the window closes. The nudge records which session owns the work so it cannot be re-derived from context. Prevents the silent work-loss pattern where a context compaction or crash wipes a session's entire in-progress diff.

title: amux IaC — define your entire agent team in one YAML file
description: A 'vertical' — a complete agent team with workers, groups, schedules, and skills — can now be declared as a single YAML file and applied with `amux iac apply vertical.yaml`. The operation is idempotent: run it again and amux reconciles to the desired state without duplication. Enables GitOps workflows for AI engineering teams: version-control your agent configuration, apply it on any machine, diff it like any other infra.

title: Worker model and token spend — visible per session in the dashboard
description: Each worker now reports its active model name and running token spend directly to the harness. The dashboard shows these alongside the worker card so you can see at a glance which agents are on Claude Sonnet vs Opus, and how much each has consumed this session. Useful for managing costs across a large fleet with mixed model tiers.

title: Message delivery verdict — know when your send actually landed
description: When you send a message to a session, the submission verdict — delivered, queued, or failed — is now recorded in the store and displayed in the Messages tab. Previously a send that failed silently looked identical to one that succeeded. Now every message has a visible outcome, and the history shows whether it reached the target session.

title: Smart tag suggestions — based on what your board is actually about
description: Tag suggestions in the board are now driven by `GET /api/board/themes` — the server's analysis of what themes the current board covers — rather than a static list. Suggestions surface the groups and topics already active in your fleet, so tagging a new card connects it to real ongoing work rather than guessing from a generic vocabulary.

title: Column gates are now enforced when edited in the UI
description: Editing a column gate through the board UI now actually enforces the new definition on subsequent transitions. Previously a gate edited in the UI was stored but not applied — agents could move cards past a gate that the board showed as active. The fix closes the gap between what the UI displays and what the server enforces.

title: Worker status card — 'working' now shows what the agent is actually doing
description: The worker card used to show a generic 'working' label whenever a session was active. It now surfaces the actual current task — the board card title or the active prompt — so you can scan the fleet at a glance and see what each agent is working on without opening their terminal.

title: Groups at a glance — every team, one tap to open
description: The Groups tab now shows every named group as a collapsed card: member count, active/idle/waiting split, board doing/todo counts, and schedule counts — all visible at once. Click a group to open all its sessions in the dashboard simultaneously. Organize your agent fleet into teams (frontend, infra, gtm, customers) and switch context between them in one tap.

title: Tag-scoped board — board list now says when it is showing a subset
description: When you fetch the board filtered by tag, the response now includes an X-Amux-Scope header so CLI tools and API callers know they are seeing a scoped view, not the full board. Eliminates the ambiguity where a filtered list and an empty global board looked identical.

title: Startup banner — YOUR TODO count now matches what pickup actually queues
description: The YOUR TODO banner on startup was showing up to 199 items when pickup queues only held 9 real candidates — it filtered on status and session while pickup also required agent ownership and active status. The banner now uses the same predicate as pickup, so the number you see is the number that matters.

title: Owner digest — push and iMessage when something is waiting on you
description: When sessions are rate-limited, waiting for your approval, or have board items stuck at done-but-unverified, amux now sends a push notification and an iMessage to your phone listing exactly what needs attention. Includes a nudge to drive done items to verified once you confirm them running in production.

title: Activity log — full tool call payloads, searchable
description: The Activity tab now shows the complete request and response payload for every tool call your agents make. Payloads expand inline via accordion, and a search bar filters across all of them. Find the tool call that slowed an agent, read exactly what arguments it passed, and see what it got back — without digging through tmux scrollback.

title: Board safety — cross-lane destruction now requires authorization
description: Closing or discarding another session's board cards now requires an authorized_by field. amux records whose word the action was taken on. Previously, cross-lane destructive mutations left no trace — now every one is auditable and attributed.

title: Watch cards now actually watch — armed watches have a real monitor
description: Previously, marking a watch card armed was a label with no listener attached — nothing evaluated the condition. Watch cards now have an active monitor that evaluates their condition and fires when it is met. Armed means monitored.

title: New board filters: is:armed and is:armedstale
description: Two new board query filters surface the watch cards your fleet is monitoring. is:armed lists every watch card currently armed and listening. is:armedstale finds watches that were armed but have gone quiet without firing. Run these to audit your tripwires without scrolling the full board.

title: Board list — server-side filters cut CLI payload from 4.7MB to instant
description: The board list endpoint now filters server-side. Instead of the CLI downloading 4.7MB of JSON and filtering locally, you pass query parameters (status, type, tag, owner, session) and receive only the matching cards. Large boards are now fast; CLI startup is no longer a network bottleneck.

title: CLI PATH mismatch — amux now says out loud when the wrong binary is on PATH
description: When amux generates a CLI binary that does not match what `which amux` resolves to, it now prints a clear warning. Previously the wrong version could silently run with no indication — this surfaces the mismatch immediately so you know which binary is actually executing.

title: Read aloud — listen to your AI agents via Piper TTS, free and local
description: amux now includes a read-aloud button on every session card and in the Trends summary, powered by Piper TTS — a free, open-source, offline text-to-speech engine. No API key, no cloud service, no per-character cost. Install Piper (brew install piper or pip install piper-tts), enable in Settings → Audio, and tap the speaker icon to hear agent output spoken aloud. Streams audio to the iOS app and mobile PWA so you can hear your morning briefing while getting ready — no screen required.

title: Gemini CLI parity — memory bridge, same-context review guard, alert help
description: Gemini CLI sessions now have full parity with Claude lanes: the shared memory bridge (notes shared across sessions) works for Gemini CLI sessions, same-context review refusal prevents a session from reviewing its own work, and the owner alert is guarded with help text to prevent misuse. This makes Gemini CLI a first-class runtime in mixed-model fleets — high-context batch tasks assigned to Gemini CLI, complex reasoning to Claude Code, both coordinating through the same board and memory system.

title: Gemini CLI state detection — Gemini lanes now visible to every status loop
description: Gemini CLI sessions were invisible to the amux status detection loop — amux couldn't tell whether they were waiting, thinking, or idle, so the watchdog couldn't self-heal them and the dashboard showed incorrect status. This fix extends state detection to the Gemini CLI provider. Gemini CLI sessions now show live status (waiting/thinking/idle/stuck) in the dashboard and receive the same watchdog coverage as Claude Code sessions.

title: Server startup 13 seconds faster — log streaming no longer blocks binding
description: The amux server was hanging for 13 seconds on startup before binding to its port — caused by _attach_log_streaming running synchronously in the main thread before the HTTP server started. Moving it to a background thread eliminates the delay. The server now binds and becomes ready to accept connections immediately on startup.

title: Rate-limit recovery — parked sessions no longer receive stray keypresses every 15s
description: The rate-limit scanner was re-pressing '1' every 15 seconds into sessions that had already dismissed the rate-limit menu and were parked waiting. This caused spurious input into idle sessions and could interfere with agents in a paused state. The scanner now correctly detects already-parked sessions and stops sending keystrokes once the menu is dismissed.

title: Trends view — see what your AI team accomplished, grouped into themes
description: The Messages tab's Trends view now answers what/who/status/needs-you per theme — no more scrolling through individual messages to understand what your AI team worked on. Each theme row shows counts of tasks queued, in progress, done, and blocked on you, with evidence links to the underlying board cards and sessions. This replaces the flat message log with a team-level view of actual work.

title: Session tab customizer — hide, show, and reorder tabs in the peek panel
description: Every tab in the session peek panel (Messages, Board, Files, Costs, and more) can now be hidden, shown, or reordered — using the same drag-and-drop customizer as the main dashboard tab bar. Only the Terminal tab is fixed. Your layout persists across sessions. If you never use the Costs tab or always want Messages first, set it once and forget it.

title: Unblock everything — one-screen triage of every blocker across all sessions
description: A new Focus mode in the Review tab surfaces every card in needs-you status across all sessions into a single scrollable list. Each blocked card shows the context the agent recorded when it flagged the blocker, plus a Nudge button to respond directly — no navigating to the session. Clear a full morning's worth of blockers in under 10 minutes without opening a single individual session.

title: Review command center — blockers-first synthesis with live session data and drill-down
description: The Review tab is now an interactive command center: blockers surface first (cards waiting for you, sorted by age), followed by per-session status and per-epic progress. All data pulls live from the board and session state — no manual reporting from agents required. Click any blocker to drill into the card or session directly from the review interface.

title: Review dashboard tab — weekly synthesis, totals, epic digest, and per-lane table
description: A dedicated Review tab now appears in the main dashboard. It shows a rolling 7-day synthesis across your entire AI team: total messages processed, total tokens spent with cost estimate, per-epic card counts broken out by status (todo/doing/done/verified), and a blockers section. Generated automatically from the board and message history — no prompt needed, readable in under 60 seconds from your phone.

title: Fleet org chart — see your AI team as a live org chart grouped by department
description: The Graph tab now has a Notes / Fleet switch. Fleet view projects all live sessions as an org chart, grouped into departments by name prefix (backend-*, frontend-* etc.). Each node shows the session's live status dot and the board card it's currently working on. Click any node to open that session's peek panel. Department colors use a validated palette that passes contrast and color-vision-deficiency checks. Node layout persists across refreshes.

title: Model badge updates instantly after /model switch — no more stale SONNET after switching to Opus
description: Running /model opus in a session wrote only user-type entries in the JSONL transcript — no assistant turn with a model field — so the session's model badge kept showing the previous model until the next actual response came in. For idle sessions, the badge was wrong indefinitely. The fix reads /model command entries in the same backward scan, so the badge updates the moment you switch, not after the next response.

title: Workspace file browser — read any file or directory in a session's workspace from the dashboard
description: Two new endpoints — GET /api/fs/read and /api/fs/list — let you read any file or list any directory inside a session's registered workspace directly from the amux dashboard or API. Browse source files, check generated outputs, read logs, or inspect CLAUDE.md configuration without leaving the dashboard or opening a terminal. The endpoints respect the workspace root, so agents cannot traverse outside their registered directory.

title: Burst view — see exactly what work was done in response to a message
description: The Messages tab now shows which board card(s) were created or updated in response to each message you sent — a direct answer to 'what happened to what I asked.' Cards spawned by a prompt appear inline next to the message in a burst view. This closes the loop between instruction and outcome: instead of hunting through board history, you see the causal chain from your words to the agent's work in one place.

title: Full board audit trail — every card edit now records before-values and is readable via API
description: Every PATCH to a board card now stores the before-values alongside the change, creating an immutable audit trail in amux.db. Read a card's full edit history via GET /api/board/<id>/history — see every status transition, description update, and dependency change with timestamps and the session that made it. Useful for post-mortems, verifying that a gate was honestly satisfied, and reconstructing what a card looked like at any point in time.

title: Autostart env write fixed — workspace settings now persist across container restarts
description: The autostart configuration write was silently failing on every workspace creation in cloud environments — meaning workspaces appeared set up but did not auto-launch on container restart. The write path is now correct and verified. Workspaces configured to autostart will reliably start their sessions after any restart, deploy, or container eviction.

title: Autonomy capture marker moved to append-only log — spurious card annotations no longer re-arm themselves
description: When an agent annotated a card it had already processed, the in-memory capture marker was being reset, causing the same card to be re-annotated on the next autonomy tick — creating duplicate cards and noisy board state. The marker now lives in the append-only session log, so it survives restarts and cannot be reset by a card mutation. Agents that previously created duplicate board cards in burst mode will no longer do so.

title: Mobile kanban board — column snap, swipe between columns, live peek on tap
description: The amux kanban board now works fully on mobile: columns snap-scroll horizontally, tapping a card opens a full peek of its details and history, stub columns stay visible so you always see all four states, and offscreen cards are virtualized for smooth scrolling on large boards. Manage your AI engineering team sprint from your phone — no laptop required.

title: Board cards now support task dependencies and reviewer assignments
description: Cards on the amux board now carry depends_on and reviewer graph edges, and the session loop traverses them. A card with depends_on waits for its dependency to reach done before becoming claimable. A card with a reviewer set gates its own completion on that reviewer's sign-off. Use depends_on to sequence agent work and reviewer to require a human check before a card closes.

title: Every incoming prompt automatically decomposes into one board card per task
description: When a session receives a prompt that contains more than one distinct task, amux now creates one board card per unit of work rather than folding everything into a single card. Each card can be honestly done or not done, gated and tracked independently. Sessions that previously accumulated 450+ tasks in one journal card will now decompose incoming work into real, actionable cards.

title: Board card API fixed — GET /api/board/<id> now returns the card that exists
description: GET /api/board/<id> was answering 'not found' for every card, including cards that clearly existed. The lookup was matching on the wrong column. Any integration that fetches individual cards by ID — the iOS app, session loops, external tooling — was broken. This is now fixed and the endpoint returns the correct card data.

title: Gmail reconnect works again — a fresh OAuth grant clears the negative cache
description: When a Gmail account hit invalid_grant (token expired or revoked), amux was caching the error and blocking subsequent OAuth attempts even after a fresh grant was issued. Re-authorizing a Gmail account now clears the negative cache immediately, so the new token is used on the next send. Affected users who were stuck in a loop of re-authenticating without success should now find reconnection works on the first attempt.

title: Ping button in the connection modal measures real round-trip latency to your amux server
description: The connection modal now has a ping button that sends 5 real HTTP requests to your amux server and reports the median round-trip time in milliseconds. Use it to verify you are connected to the right server instance, diagnose slow dashboard updates, or check latency on a mobile or remote connection. The ping bypasses the ETag/304 cache so each request is a real round trip.

title: Board polling now uses ETag/304 — 3.4MB saved per unchanged poll
description: The board polling endpoint now returns an ETag header and handles conditional GET requests with If-None-Match. When the board has not changed since the last poll, the server returns 304 Not Modified with an empty body instead of the full board JSON. In practice this saves approximately 3.4MB per poll cycle when nothing has changed — which is most of the time, especially overnight when agents are working and the board is stable. Significant for mobile users and anyone on a metered connection.

title: Messages tab now filters by kind — human, session, or schedule
description: The three-kind message filter (human / session / schedule) that was already available in the peek panel is now also on the standalone Messages tab. Filter to only see messages you sent, only inter-agent relays, or only scheduled triggers — or view all three together. Useful on the Messages tab when reviewing what happened overnight across a large fleet.

title: Browser profiles — create and use named auth sessions for automation
description: The Browser tab now shows all your saved browser profiles and lets you create new ones directly from the UI. Each profile stores its own cookie jar and authentication state, so AI browser automation tasks start already logged in — no re-entering credentials on every run. Create a 'stripe' profile, a 'github-work' profile, a 'client-acme' profile, and launch different agents with different identities simultaneously. Profiles persist across server restarts in ~/.amux/browser-profiles/.

title: Copy path button in file preview — one click to copy a file's bare path
description: The file preview overlay now has a dedicated 'Path' button next to 'Copy' and 'Link'. Clicking it copies the file's bare relative path to clipboard — useful when you want to reference a file in a steering message, a script, or another tool without the full deep-link URL. The underlying clipboard + toast logic was refactored into a shared helper so both Path and Link use the same fallback and toast behavior. Contributed by @Dygreens in PR #64.

title: MKV and HEVC video files now play in the Files tab
description: MKV files (including HEVC/H.265 codec) were showing 'Format not supported by this browser' instead of playing. The bug was a one-liner: the video player was extracting the file extension from the API URL path (/api/file/raw) instead of from the 'path=' query parameter — so ext was always 'raw', bypassing the ffmpeg transcoding path. Fixed. MKV files now correctly route through the background MP4 prepare job with progress indicator, and fall back to live-transcode for desktop browsers when the cache is empty.

title: Service worker caches the app shell — 1.6 MB saved on every reload
description: The amux dashboard's app shell (HTML, CSS, JS) was being re-fetched from the server on every page load — 1.6 MB of network traffic per visit. The service worker now caches the shell on first install and serves it from cache on subsequent loads. Result: sub-100ms dashboard loads on repeat visits, even on slow mobile connections. The service worker also now correctly installs over the self-signed TLS certificate used for localhost development.

title: Fix: browser profile picker crash and localStorage quota error
description: Two bugs in the browser profiles UI were fixed: (1) opening the browser tab with no profiles created caused a crash in the profile picker dropdown; (2) saving a large browser session state to localStorage was throwing a quota exceeded error, which could silently prevent profile saves. The profile picker now gracefully renders an empty state, and profile data is no longer stored in localStorage (moved to server-side storage via ~/.amux/browser-profiles/).

title: Session tabs sorted by frequency — find your active sessions instantly
description: The peek panel's tab order now reflects how often you actually reach for each tab. High-frequency live tabs (Terminal, Steering, Messages, Dictation) move to the front; lower-frequency reference tabs (Transcript, Worktree, Commits) move to the back. New order: Terminal, Steering, Schedules, Messages, Dictation, Board, Notes, Cost, Transcript, Commits, Worktree. The Dictation tab also gets a badge when you're recording, so you can see which sessions are actively receiving voice input at a glance.

title: Local Whisper dictation — 12× faster, works fully offline
description: amux's voice dictation now runs local Whisper transcription on-device instead of sending audio to a cloud API. The result is a 12× speed improvement (measured on 4 realistic amux dictations) and full offline capability — dictate to your agents on a plane, in a dead zone, or anywhere without internet. Deterministic session name recovery replaces the previous probabilistic match, eliminating misrouted messages. The fallback to cloud Whisper is still available for devices that prefer it.

title: Persistent dictation outbox — never lose a voice message again (v0.9.202)
description: v0.9.202 fixes the most painful dictation failure: a server-side error (Gemini hiccup, quota limit, bad API key) previously caused the recorded audio to be silently discarded. Re-recording was the only option. Now, every recorded audio clip is saved to a persistent outbox before transmission. If the send fails for any reason — network drop, server error, quota — the clip stays in the outbox and you can retry the exact same take. No re-recording, no lost messages.

title: PWA screen restore: return to exactly where you left off after iOS evicts the app (v0.9.189)
description: When iOS evicts a backgrounded PWA and you return, the dashboard now restores the active tab and the open session peek panel — exactly where you left off. Previously, any iOS app eviction reset the view to the default Sessions tab with no peek open, forcing you to navigate back manually. State is persisted to sessionStorage on every change and applied before the first render on reload.

title: Opus 5 support: claude-opus-5 and claude-opus-5[1m] added to all model pickers (v0.9.187)
description: Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5) and its 1-million-token context variant (claude-opus-5[1m]) are now available in all three model pickers: session config modal, edit-field inline picker, and new-session wizard. Opus 5 sits at the top of the list. The CLI accepts --model claude-opus-5 and routes correctly to the model class.

title: Map: distance/near-me sort + GeoJSON and CSV export-import
description: Map pins now sort by distance from your current location (near-me mode). Export your entire map as GeoJSON or CSV; re-import either format to share collections between devices or teammates. Distance sort uses the browser Geolocation API and falls back gracefully when permission is denied.

title: Map: two-tone pin color for 2nd tag + marker clustering
description: Map pins now display a two-tone color: primary tag sets the fill, secondary tag sets a contrasting stroke. When many pins are in the same area, they cluster into a count bubble that expands on click. Clustering keeps the map readable at city scale without losing individual markers.

title: Map: AND-mode tag filter + richer Places capture
description: Tag filtering now supports AND mode — show only pins that match ALL selected tags (previously OR-only). The Places capture panel now pulls richer metadata from Google Places: rating, price level, opening hours, website, and phone number, all stored with the pin.

title: Silent-crash self-heal: sessions with a dead Claude process now restart themselves, no CC_AUTO_CONTINUE required
description: A Claude process killed by SIGKILL, OOM, or a crash (pane goes blank as Claude tears down its alternate-screen buffer) now self-heals unconditionally. Previously, both auto-restart paths required CC_AUTO_CONTINUE opt-in, so sessions without it sat dead forever. The watchdog now distinguishes a crash (no Claude child, pane not a clean shell prompt) from an intentional /exit (clean shell prompt) and restarts only the former. Crash-loop cap: 3 crashes in 15 minutes → stop + alert.

title: AskUserQuestion blocking: selector-parked sessions surface the block instead of silently holding inbound messages
description: When a session is parked at an AskUserQuestion or tool-approval selector, it can't safely receive an inter-session message (typing there + Escape would reject the pending tool). amux correctly queues the message — but previously gave no signal that the session was blocked. Now the selector head-of-line block is surfaced in the UI so you know why your message is waiting.

title: gzip all text responses + ETag/304 + gzip SSE stream — v0.9.183
description: All text/HTML, JSON, and CSS/JS responses are now gzip-compressed when the client supports it. Static assets get ETag + 304 Not Modified support so unchanged files don't re-download. The SSE event stream itself is also gzip-compressed (chunked transfer encoding), cutting mobile data usage for long-running sessions. Measured 60-80% payload reduction on dashboard load.

title: Allow 'x' key in terminal — kills hung subagents in Claude Code
description: The 'x' key was being intercepted by the dashboard before reaching the terminal, preventing users from killing hung Claude Code subagents (the standard interrupt gesture). Now passes through correctly. Also fixes a regression where Ctrl+C was occasionally dropped during rapid key sequences.

title: Scheduler now logs who created or deleted each schedule — full audit trail
description: Every schedule create and delete is now recorded with attribution — who created it (by session name or IP), what session it runs in, and when. The audit trail appears in the scheduler's run history. Useful for debugging 'who scheduled this?' and for team setups where multiple agents manage shared schedules.

title: Shared-checkout guard protects your staged files when agents try to check out the same branch
description: When multiple agents try to git checkout the same branch simultaneously, the new staged-state guard detects the conflict and holds — preventing a checkout from stomping your in-progress staged files. Also detects and reports orphaned rebase states left behind by crashed agents. Pairs with git worktree isolation for maximum parallel-agent safety.

title: Click any message to insert it into the terminal, or copy it — with a locate button
description: The Messages tab now has per-message actions: a click-to-insert button switches to the Terminal tab and pastes the message into the input composer, a copy button copies to clipboard, and a locate button jumps to the message's source in the session output. Speeds up replay, iterating on past prompts, and finding where a specific message landed in the transcript.

title: Pending messages visible as ⏳ in the Messages tab while offline
description: Messages sent while the device is offline now appear immediately in the Messages tab with a ⏳ pending indicator. A composer pill shows 'N unsent messages queued' until the connection is restored and they deliver. Previously, offline-queued messages were invisible until delivery — making it unclear whether your send had registered. Works on mobile PWA and native iOS app.

title: Session output restored for API integrations — peek endpoint was returning empty
description: The /api/sessions/<name>/peek endpoint was missing the output field in its response, causing all API integrations and the autopilot sensor to see empty output from every session. Now restored. If you're using the REST API to read session output (for automation, alerts, or third-party integrations), no changes needed — the field is back.

title: Cost tab — see token spend and task attribution across your entire agent fleet
description: New Cost tab in the global dashboard and each session's peek panel shows token spend, cost breakdown, and which tasks consumed the most. The cost ledger attributes every token event to the task window that generated it, so you can see exactly what each agent worked on and what it cost. Essential for running parallel agents cost-efficiently.

title: Token/cost ledger with per-task attribution + /api/observability endpoint
description: Server-side cost ledger records every token event with task-window attribution. Query the new /api/observability endpoint to get per-session and per-task cost breakdowns programmatically. Useful for budget tracking, billing attribution, and building cost-aware automation that slows down when spend gets high.

title: The amux Mental Model guide — every surface as a knowledge-work system
description: New guide that explains every amux surface (sessions, board, notes, cost, CRM) as a unified knowledge-work system rather than a bag of features. Includes UI mocks, the design reasoning behind each surface, and a hero link from the homepage. Useful for onboarding new team members or understanding how the pieces fit together.

title: Skills menu ships four curated built-in skills — adhd, amux, handoff, standup
description: The skills chip toolbar now ships four high-quality built-in skills: /adhd (ADHD-shaped output — bullet-first, numbered steps, visible wins), /amux (dashboard orchestration commands), /handoff (structured context handoff between agents), and /standup (daily standup report generator). Each is production-tested and ready to use without any configuration.

title: /adhd skill ships by default on every fresh install
description: The /adhd skill is now seeded automatically on install — no configuration needed. It shapes all agent output to be ADHD-friendly: leads with concrete next actions, numbers multi-step work, externalizes state across turns, suppresses tangents, and makes wins visible. Trigger it on any message including coding tasks, debugging, or planning sessions.

title: WCAG-AA contrast in both themes + a labeled theme toggle button
description: Fixed contrast ratios across dark and light themes to meet WCAG AA standards — muted text, borders, and secondary elements all now pass. The theme toggle is now a visible labeled button (was an unlabeled icon), making it accessible to screen reader users and keyboard-only navigation. Both changes apply to the dashboard and all site pages.

title: Loading indicator when opening a session — no more blank flash
description: Sessions now show a Loading latest… spinner pill while fetching output on open. Previously there was a blank white flash that could last 1-3 seconds while the peek API responded. The spinner gives immediate visual feedback and disappears the moment output arrives.

title: HTML file previews are now fully interactive — scripts run in the iframe
description: The HTML preview in the Files tab now allows scripts to execute inside the preview iframe. Previously, inline JavaScript was silently blocked, making generated apps, charts, D3 visualizations, and interactive reports preview as broken static HTML. Now they run correctly, including React/Vue bundles, canvas animations, and PostHog-instrumented pages your agents produce.

title: Steering delivers messages in ~2s when idle — was taking up to 9s
description: Messages sent via the Steering panel now reach your agent in about 2 seconds when it's idle, down from up to 9 seconds before. The idle settle check now runs every 2s (was 4s) and queued messages dispatch immediately once an idle state is confirmed. Makes interactive agent steering feel snappy instead of sluggish.

title: Owner alerts include verified provenance — origin session and timestamp stamped server-side
description: Each alert sent to the owner (push + iMessage/SMS) now includes a server-stamped origin — the session name and timestamp are recorded server-side at send time, so the recipient can verify the alert genuinely came from the reported session. Prevents any session from spoofing another session's identity in an alert body (AMUX-1795).

title: Pressing Enter submits the suggested prompt — no more silent re-trigger of the picker
description: Tightened the Enter-key guard in the footer send bar so pressing Enter on a pre-filled suggested prompt submits it immediately instead of re-opening the autocomplete picker. Fixes a regression where Enter would bounce back to suggestion mode rather than deliver the message.

title: Hibernate no longer auto-kills sessions when only a few are running — stops unexpected context loss
description: Previously amux would auto-stop idle sessions after the hibernate threshold regardless of how many sessions were active — causing context loss when you stepped away from a solo run. Now the auto-stop only fires when MANY sessions are running simultaneously. A solo overnight run won't be killed by the hibernate watchdog.

title: "Send now" in Steering actually delivers the message — was silently re-queuing it
description: Clicking 'Send now' in the Steering panel appeared to work but was silently re-queuing the message instead of delivering it immediately. Fixed so the message is delivered on the spot when you tap Send now.

title: Steering "Sent history" is now a collapsible accordion, collapsed by default
description: The Sent history list in the Steering panel is now collapsed by default, keeping the panel clean when you open it. Click the header to expand and see past messages sent to this session.

title: Click any message in the Messages tab to copy it — with 'Copied' feedback
description: Clicking any message in the session's Messages tab now copies it to the clipboard and shows a brief 'Copied' confirmation. Useful for grabbing a past prompt to re-send or relay to another session.

title: Messages tab in the session page — full message history, one tap away
description: The session peek panel now has a Messages tab showing every message sent to or from that session — from amux send, from the Steering bar, from other sessions, from scheduled prompts. Click any message to copy it. Updates live and works on mobile.

title: Guided setup walkthrough — 8 surfaces, real flows, never clips on small screens
description: The setup walkthrough now takes you through all 8 core amux surfaces in a single linear tour: sessions, steering, schedules, board, calendar, messages, browser, and skills. Each step actually un-hides its tab and opens the real create flow (add a session, open the scheduler modal, create a board card, add a calendar event) — so the walkthrough bootstraps your command center instead of pointing at closed doors. The tooltip is now fit-and-clamped to the true visible viewport including pinch-zoom and safe-area offsets, so Skip/Back/Next never clip off screen on iPhone or small windows.

title: @ mentions now list every session with fuzzy autocomplete and match highlighting
description: Typing a bare @ in the Send/Steer bar now drops a list of all running sessions (running ones first, scrollable) so you never have to remember session names. Matching switched from prefix-only to fuzzy subsequence ranking with contiguity, word-boundary, and prefix bonuses — 'mg' matches mixpeek-general, 'gen' matches ...general. Matching characters are bolded in the accent color so you can see exactly why a session was suggested. Works in both the session send bar and the steering bar.

title: amux send CLI — inter-session messages now carry a verified server-side origin
description: Use `amux send OTHER_SESSION "your message"` from any terminal to send a message to another session with a server-stamped, unforgeable origin. The origin is set server-side from the X-Amux-Session header so the receiving session always knows which session the message truly came from — eliminating a class of mis-attribution bugs where a relay could appear to come from the wrong session. The raw `curl` fallback also works by passing `X-Amux-Session: $AMUX_SESSION` manually.

title: Git branch badge in the peek panel — see which branch your agent is on at a glance
description: The directory row in the peek panel now shows a colored git branch badge (⎇ name) pushed to the right: yellow for main, green for a feature branch, red if a conflict is detected. The badge is clickable (opens the branch popover) and updates when you open a session or on the next background poll — so you always know whether your agent drifted onto the wrong branch or forgot to create one.

title: File explorer keeps all columns on mobile — horizontal scroll instead of hiding Size/Date
description: The file explorer previously hid the Size and Modified columns on small screens, leaving you with name-only rows on phone. Now the table header and rows share a single horizontal-scroll container with a 460px minimum width — you swipe sideways to see all columns, and sortable column headers still work. This matches standard mobile data-table UX and makes the file explorer fully usable on iPhone.

title: Gmail reply now always targets the external party — never emails yourself back
description: Reply routing now excludes all connected accounts and owned domains from the recipient set, so replying to a message you sent no longer emails yourself. reply_all targets all external participants; single reply targets the external From (or To if you were the sender). Fail-closed: if no external recipient is found, the reply is refused rather than silently emailing yourself. Cross-account threading is also fixed — a thread on info@ can now be replied to from ethan@ with correct In-Reply-To / References headers.

title: Peek panel now scrolls tall tables vertically without getting stuck
description: A tall Claude-generated table rendered as a .peek-box with overflow-x:auto. The CSS spec then computed overflow-y to auto, making the box a vertical scroll container — overscroll-behavior:contain stopped that scroll from chaining to the peek body, so wheel and swipe gestures were swallowed and the table wouldn't scroll. Fixed by setting overflow-y:hidden on .peek-box (boxes are content-height, so nothing is clipped) and scoping overscroll-behavior to the X axis only.

title: Steering now holds scheduled messages until a session is idle — no more interrupted tool calls
description: Automated sends (scheduler, inter-session channels) were interrupting sessions mid-tool-call: the Escape key that clears the input line was being sent while a tool-approval or picker prompt was live, actively rejecting pending tool calls. Now: a session in 'waiting' state (live selector) is not treated as deliverable — the message parks in the steering queue until the session returns to an idle prompt. Deliberate user sends still go through immediately. Fixes a recurring issue where sessions running 11+ schedules would have tool calls killed at :00 boundaries.

title: iOS App Store updated with new screenshots — 6 views at iPhone 16 Pro Max resolution
description: Added 6 App Store screenshots rendered at 1320x2868 (3x iPhone 16 Pro Max): Sessions overview, Peek panel, Board, Calendar, Notes, and Scheduler. Screenshots were generated via Playwright at full resolution and submitted to App Store Connect.

title: iOS App Store listing optimized for search — new subtitle, keywords, and description
description: App Store listing rewritten for discoverability: subtitle, keywords (added: claude code, vibe coding, developer tools; removed: tmux, ssh, copilot), description, and promotional text. Description now leads with benefits and concrete use cases rather than feature lists.

title: Board task ownership is now auditable — shepherd vs executor split
description: Board issues now track two distinct roles: the session that created/delegated the task (shepherd) and the session actively executing it. A no-executor tripwire prevents tasks from sitting in 'doing' without an active owner — stale doing items surface immediately in the board UI.

title: Stale 'doing' detector — board tasks can't be silently hoarded
description: The kanban board now flags any task that's been in 'doing' for too long without progress updates. Tasks can't be held indefinitely — the detector makes it hard for an agent or session to claim a task and then go quiet, keeping the board a reliable source of truth.

title: Messages tab — your AI team's full communication history in one place
description: A new global Messages tab shows every message sent between sessions, newest first. Click 'Locate in peek' to jump to any message in the sending agent's terminal context. Finally: a Slack-like history view for your AI engineering team's inter-agent coordination.

title: Install via Homebrew or PyPI — no manual setup required
description: amux is now on Homebrew (`brew install mixpeek/amux/amux`) and PyPI (`pipx install amux`). Zero-install trial available with `uvx amux serve` — no git clone, no install.sh. The classic `./install.sh` path remains for self-hosting on servers.

title: Steering delivery is faster and less noisy — batched nudges with a cap
description: Steering instructions are now batched before delivery, a per-session nudge cap prevents over-steering runaway loops, and task-label updates are throttled so the dashboard stays readable when many agents are active. Net result: cleaner steering, less token waste.

title: Duplicate form submissions no longer send the same message twice
description: A race between post-submit verification and a torn network request could cause the same steering message or board update to submit twice. Fixed with a submit-lock that clears only after the server confirms receipt.

title: Tab order stays stable when you show or hide tabs
description: Hiding and re-showing a tab (Proxies, Skills, Database, etc.) no longer creates a duplicate. Tab positions are deduplicated on update so your layout stays exactly where you left it.

title: Database tab — full SQL workbench for your agent data
description: The SQL tab is now the Database tab with a full workbench UX: schema browser on the left, query editor, and a formatted results table. Query your sessions, board issues, schedules, CRM, and notes directly with SQL.

title: SQL workbench — query amux.db directly from the dashboard
description: New SQL tab connects directly to amux.db (SQLite). Run any read query against sessions, board_issues, notes, schedules, cal_events, and crm_contacts — results appear instantly in the dashboard.

title: Terminal tab fills the full viewport with a clean toolbar
description: The terminal tab now expands to fill your entire screen — no more wasted space. A new toolbar above shows the session name, status indicator, and quick-action buttons, leaving the full viewport for output.

title: Skills tab — model-agnostic slash commands sync across all sessions
description: The Skills tab (now its own dedicated dashboard tab) shows all your custom slash commands. Skills are model-agnostic: the same /commit, /review, or /deploy skill works whether the session runs Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Gemini CLI. Cross-provider sync means new sessions pick them up automatically.

title: Steering tab shows a history of steers you've delivered
description: The steering panel now shows every instruction you've sent to that session, newest first. Scroll back to see the full steering history without digging through transcript logs.

title: Peek lookup uses your session's provider on its fastest model
description: The peek lookup feature (quick AI answer about a session's output) now automatically uses the same provider as the session and routes to that provider's fastest model, so lookups are as quick as possible without switching context.

title: Send-keys lands on the active pane in tmux 3.7b
description: tmux 3.7b changed how send-keys targets panes when no pane is specified. amux now always targets the session's active pane explicitly, so amux send and all send-keys operations work correctly on tmux 3.7b+.

title: Steering queue waits for the agent to settle before delivering
description: When you queue a message for a running agent (via the steering bar or saved chips), amux now waits for the agent to actually go idle before delivering it — instead of injecting the text immediately, which could interrupt the agent mid-thought. The settle window (default 6s, configurable via AMUX_STEER_SETTLE_S) checks that the agent's output has been quiet before delivery. This prevents the common failure mode where a steering instruction arrives while the agent is mid-tool-call and gets ignored or corrupts the input buffer.

title: Security hardening — XSS, CSRF, DOMPurify, and RCE patches (v0.9.97–v0.9.98)
description: Five security patches shipped in a batch: (1) Notes and markdown content are now sanitized with DOMPurify before DOM insertion — a malicious note couldn't inject scripts. (2) Email HTML is rendered in a sandboxed iframe with no scripting allowed. (3) Attribute values are server-side escaped to close reflected XSS vectors. (4) A CSRF guard now rejects state-changing API calls from cross-origin sources. (5) Path traversal, write escalation, and git argument injection vectors were closed — an attacker with API access couldn't write outside the allowed directory or inject shell arguments via git endpoints. These patches apply to all amux users. Update recommended.

title: Tunnel rate limiting — your tunneled service is protected from traffic spikes
description: The amux tunnel proxy now enforces a per-connection rate limit on the requests it forwards to your local service. Previously, anyone who discovered a tunnel URL (or deliberately tested it) could hammer your local server with rapid requests — your development server had no built-in protection. Now the relay throttles incoming connections, giving your local service breathing room. The rate limit is applied at the relay layer, before traffic reaches your machine. This is part of the Proxies feature (v0.9.95+, accessible from the new Proxies tab in the dashboard).

title: Proxies now a first-class dashboard tab — manage your tunnels from the UI
description: The tunnel/proxies feature is now accessible from a dedicated tab in the amux dashboard tab bar. Previously, tunnels were managed only via CLI or API. The new Proxies tab shows all active proxy configurations, their public URLs, and status. The file list row context menu also got a positioning fix — it now appears next to the button rather than in a fixed position, so it's no longer clipped on smaller screens or partially off-screen. SW v0.9.95.

title: Peek reflows to your screen — no more double-wrapped text on phones
description: The peek panel (session terminal output) now measures the viewer's real character width and tells tmux to resize the pane to match. Previously, panes were always sized for a wide desktop terminal (~220 cols), so phones and narrow windows got double-wrapped text and horizontal scrolling. Claude Code reflows the entire transcript on terminal resize, so the fix is automatic: peek probes the viewport, sends the measured width, and Claude Code's output reformats itself to fit. Desktop gets the full-width view; phones get a clean, narrow layout. SW v0.9.85.

title: Tap agent rows to switch transcript in peek
description: The ⏺/◯ agent panel rows in the peek terminal are now tappable: tap a row to switch the transcript view to that agent. Previously, navigating between the main agent and subagents required using the ▲/▼ buttons. Now a single tap on any agent row switches the view, making subagent navigation much faster on both desktop and mobile. Combined with the ▲/▼ buttons and ⌂ home button, you have three ways to navigate between transcripts in a multi-subagent session. SW v0.9.83.

title: Load earlier output — scroll back through the complete session log
description: The peek panel now has a 'Load earlier output' bar at the top that fetches older log pages and prepends them above the live terminal view. Previously, the peek panel only showed what was currently in the tmux scroll buffer — if Claude Code had written thousands of lines over a long session, most of that history was inaccessible from the dashboard. Now you can page backward through the complete session log without attaching to a terminal. Each page load fetches the previous chunk of the log file and inserts it above what was already showing. SW v0.9.82.

title: Subagent switcher — navigate between main agent and subagent transcripts in peek
description: When Claude Code spawns subagents (for parallel subtasks or in agentic loops), you can now switch between their transcripts directly in the peek panel. Use the ▲/▼ buttons to step through prev/next agents, or tap any agent row in the panel to jump directly to that transcript. The ⌂ button always returns you to the main agent's output. Previously, the only way to see a subagent's output was to attach to the tmux pane, which required knowing the session name and navigating tmux pane splitting. The subagent switcher makes multi-agent debugging accessible from any browser or the iOS app. SW v0.9.79.

title: Mobile terminal logs — full peek output on phone without losing the bottom nav
description: The peek panel (session terminal logs) on mobile now reclaims the full Chrome viewport. Previously, iOS Chrome showed the address bar and bottom toolbar even in PWA mode, cutting off several rows of log output and making it impossible to see the most recent agent output. The new layout adjusts for the browser chrome dynamically, giving you the maximum usable screen for logs. This makes phone-based agent monitoring substantially more practical during active sessions.

title: Per-session token breakdown in the dashboard header
description: The token counter in the amux logo modal now shows a per-session breakdown instead of a per-directory aggregate. Previously, if you had multiple sessions registered to the same directory, their token usage was lumped together and credited to whichever session happened to be listed first. Now each session shows its own running total independently. Useful for teams running parallel agents on the same repo who want to track which session is consuming the most context.

title: Connection history modal — click the Live pill to see past disconnections
description: Clicking the connection status indicator (the green 'live' pill in the dashboard header) now opens a Connection modal that shows your browser client's full disconnection history for this session. Each degradation episode — polling, offline — is listed with start and end timestamps, duration, and whether it's ongoing. History survives page reloads (localStorage-backed) and a Clear button resets it. Useful for diagnosing flaky connections, understanding gaps in live output, and confirming how long your phone was offline while an overnight agent was running.

title: Start agent sessions in background — amux start --detach / -d
description: amux start now accepts --detach (or -d) to create a session without attaching to your terminal. The command starts the agent and returns immediately (exit 0), leaving your shell free. Previously, amux start always attached — blocking scripts, justfiles, SSH one-shots, and CI pipelines that had no terminal to attach to.
